title: Artifact byte checksums
text: API: md5 gives the exact contract. artifact_checksum::md5 computes the sixteen MD5 digest bytes for a byte slice. The artifact parser uses this legacy checksum for its Z-card check. The Z card is the artifact checksum record. It does not select repository content identities. SHA-1 and SHA3 remain in content_hash. Structural parsing has its own explicit limits and validation rules. Md5Checksum::new starts an owned computation. update appends the complete slice, including zero bytes and bytes outside UTF-8. Empty updates do nothing. finish consumes the computation and returns [u8; 16]. Each value has fixed memory use and can be interleaved with other computations. No input copy, file access or process-global state is required. Slice lengths bound each call. The caller chooses how much data to supply. There is no artifact size policy or cancellation mechanism in this byte primitive. use gossil::artifact_checksum::{md5, Md5Checksum}; let mut checksum = Md5Checksum::new(); checksum.update(b"a"); checksum.update(b"bc"); assert_eq!(checksum.finish(), md5(b"abc"));

title: Artifact byte checksums
text: The inspected Fossil mirror is b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The native build reports 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. In src/manifest.c, verify_z_card hashes the bytes before the final 35-byte Z card through md5sum_init, md5sum_step_text and md5sum_finish. This module supplies that checksum operation. It does not inspect a Z card. The byte result maps to md5sum_blob in src/md5.c. The incremental operations map to the positive-length and zero-length byte behavior of md5sum_step_text. Rust ownership replaces the native shared context and overwritten static result. The consuming finish requires a fresh value for another computation. It does not reproduce the native implicit reset. Negative lengths and C string scanning are excluded. md5sum_step_blob needs no separate Rust adapter because slices already describe bytes and length. Excluded native functions are md5sum_current_state, md5sum_file and md5sum_test. md5sum_current_state sums words of the internal context for troubleshooting. Its two callers in vfile.c are commented out. It is not a snapshot of the MD5 digest. The native command and filesystem behaviors, repository R-card aggregation, ETags and all artifact producers remain outside this module. Native MD5Init, MD5Update, MD5Final, MD5Transform and DigestToBase16 are not translated into Rust here. The implementation uses RustCrypto’s exact-pinned md-5 version 0.10.6. This version shares the existing digest 0.10 dependency with SHA-2. The lockfile records its registry checksum. Its versioned documentation describes the API used here. RustCrypto’s current documentation identifies legacy interoperability as the purpose of MD5. This module adds no identity or security policy and forwards no computation to C.

title: Artifact byte checksums

title: Artifact parser
text: API: parse_artifact and parse_artifact_with_usage give the exact contracts. The artifact module parses all eight Fossil structural artifact types with explicit resource limits. The types are manifest, cluster, control, wiki, ticket, attachment, technote and forum. A card is a record in the artifact byte format. The parser takes bytes and returns an owned result with read-only access to parsed fields. It keeps the original input, including any signature envelope. It does not require valid UTF-8.

title: Artifact parser
text: Call parse_artifact(input, limits, dates).await with a ParseLimits value chosen for the calling operation. Set each field explicitly, including input_bytes, cards, owned_bytes and entries. All four fields have type usize. The byte fields count bytes, and the other fields count cards and list entries. There is no default policy. The owned-byte limit counts logical charges for retained input, encoded tokens, copies and list entries. Allocations use fallible reservation. A resource failure is separate from malformed input, checksum mismatch and a date-provider failure.

title: Artifact parser
text: For several artifacts in one operation, call parse_artifact_with_usage(input, limits, dates).await. It returns the same parsed result with a ParseUsage value on success. The original parse_artifact function delegates to this implementation and returns only the parsed result. ParseUsage reports charges against each limit. input_bytes counts the full raw input, including a recognized signature envelope. cards counts nonzero card markers consumed by the structural loop, including Z and repeated empty P cards. A trailing zero marker consumes its delimiter without adding a card. Body newlines and envelope lines do not add cards. owned_bytes reports all charged bytes, including retained raw input, copies, encoded token lengths charged before decoding, and the size of inserted list entries. The counters report logical charges against ParseLimits; they do not measure every physical Rust allocator byte. This charge can exceed the decoded output length. It also includes allocations for tokens later discarded, such as reserved file paths. entries counts list insertions; empty P cards add none. Subtract successful usage from the operation’s remaining limits before the next call. Each call checks those remaining limits before its charged allocations. Usage is returned only on success. A caller that needs an atomic operation must stop on any error and discard its operation state. The parser does not maintain the aggregate budget or remember earlier failures. The API example parses a cluster and subtracts all four successful charges from a caller-owned budget. The private recording library borrows one parser work ledger across its complete repository operation. Other callers remain responsible for their own aggregate accounting.

title: Artifact parser
text: Implement DateProvider on the operation’s selected SQLite/libSQL owner. The local storage guide explains transaction ownership. Its asynchronous julianday method can borrow a transaction. It receives an optional raw token already truncated by the parser at its native C-string boundary, and returns an optional Julian day. A NULL result acts as zero and fails date validation. Provider execution errors retain their original cause. A constant date adapter can isolate grammar tests, but it cannot qualify date compatibility. The result exposes decoded comments and users, manifest files and parents, tags, ticket fields and cluster members. It also exposes attachment fields, wiki and forum fields, body bytes and converted dates. D cards carry artifact dates, and E cards carry event dates. Their raw date tokens remain available. Callers cannot construct or mutate a validated result through this API.

title: Artifact parser
text: The port follows Fossil manifest.c:467-1153 and its eight allowed/required card masks at lines 129-138. The pinned Fossil UUID is 7e8ecf0ce4a3c05aa39de7ffe2828d23e334efe446ef2387e09f205ef00b2227. Fossil’s source is copyright D. Richard Hipp under the Simplified BSD License. The parser checks the exact MD5 before decoding a recognized final Z record. It strips recognized PGP and SSH envelopes for parsing and checksum purposes. Envelope stripping does not verify a signature’s authenticity. The pinned card matrix requires Z even for manifests. R validates hexadecimal syntax. Repository file checksum verification belongs to storage. Tokens stop at space, LF or raw NUL. Each card consumes tokens as its native branch does. A raw NUL can be an intermediate delimiter in some cards. It is not subject to a blanket acceptance rule. Decoded tokens retain bytes after an escaped NUL, together with the length visible to C consumers. A zero card marker ends the native card loop after consuming its space or LF delimiter. Parsing succeeds only if that cursor reaches the end and the earlier cards satisfy the type rules. Unread bytes after the marker still fail. The W scanner uses unsigned 32-bit modular arithmetic and the native new < old overflow branch. It checks the remaining input before copying body bytes. Decimal suffixes and empty digit sequences follow the source branch. Manifest file paths use the legacy nonstrict rules. Paths must be nonempty and have no empty, dot or dot-dot slash-separated components. Unicode and backslash restrictions are not imposed. Reserved filenames are suppressed after comparison with the last retained filename. The parser retains repeated empty P cards, native type inference, tag ordering, forum postconditions and the historical technote P-before-N exception. Attachment basenames follow the compiled platform’s directory separator rule. Windows behavior remains unqualified.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: API: pack gives the exact contract. The library has Fossil byte digests and packed-blob operations. Packing adds a capacity header to compressed bytes. These primitives do not select a repository hash policy or store content. The runner and these primitives share a crate. CLI integration remains separate work. Legacy MD5 checksums have a separate artifact checksum module. The artifact parser uses that module for Z-card validation. The checksum module does not select repository content identities.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: use gossil::{compression, content_hash}; let digest = content_hash::sha1(b"abc"); assert_eq!(digest.len(), 20); let packed = compression::pack(b"abc", -1).unwrap(); assert_eq!(compression::unpack(&packed, 3).unwrap(), compression::Unpacked::Bytes(b"abc".to_vec())); In the example, -1 selects the default compression level, and 3 limits decoded output to three bytes. sha1(input: &[u8]) returns [u8; 20]. pack(input: &[u8], level: i32) returns Result , BlobError>. unpack(input: &[u8], max_output: usize) returns Result . See the runner prerequisites for actual tool setup.

title: Byte digests and packed blobs
text: The port follows Fossil Git revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The source surfaces are src/blob.c:1372–1535, src/sha1.c:185–201, and src/sha3.c:385–468,591–606,622–679, and the SHA1DC initialization in src/sha1hard.c:1327–1342. content_hash::sha1 accepts arbitrary bytes and returns twenty digest bytes. SHA1DC detects known SHA1 collision attacks. It preserves Fossil’s collision detection and safe-hash defaults. For a known collision attack, it returns the mitigated digest. The byte helper ignores the separate collision indication, as sha1sum_blob does. It does not return the ordinary vulnerable digest for those inputs. content_hash::sha3 accepts each width from 128 through 512 in steps of 32. It returns the corresponding binary digest, or None for an unsupported width. content_hash::hex renders bytes as lowercase hexadecimal. SHA3 uses Fossil’s width-dependent capacity and its 0x06 and 0x80 padding. The small adapter handles byte absorption, padding and extraction in explicit little-endian lane order. The maintained keccak crate supplies the permutation. A shorter digest is not a truncated standard-width hash. The four standard widths use FIPS-202 padding. The other widths preserve Fossil’s extensions. compression::pack accepts zlib levels -1 and zero through nine. Level -1 selects the backend default. compression::pack_two compresses the concatenated slices at level nine, as Fossil does. Neither operation allocates a concatenated input buffer. The compressed representation can differ between backends. A packed blob contains a four-byte unsigned big-endian capacity followed by a zlib stream. The capacity is an upper bound on decoded bytes. A larger header than the actual output is valid. Bytes following the first complete zlib stream are ignored. Invalid checksums, incomplete streams and output exceeding the header produce errors. compression::unpack accepts a caller-selected limit. It rejects a header above that limit before decoding, then checks each output chunk against the header. Output grows through fallible reservations. The caller sets the limit. The format has no additional fixed small cap. Encoding rejects lengths above the unsigned 32-bit header range. C overflow and undefined behavior are not ported. Inputs of at most four bytes produce Unpacked::NoPayload. A caller that replaces an existing buffer must leave its existing buffer contents unchanged for that result. A successfully decoded empty stream produces Unpacked::Bytes with an empty vector. These outcomes differ. Fossil’s diagnostic test-uncompress ignores the C function’s error return, so CLI exit zero does not prove successful decoding. Allocation and compression errors retain their underlying causes. Digest results have a fixed small size. Compressed input and output remain caller-owned. The API does not define database, filesystem, publication or privacy behavior.

title: CLI reference
text: The gossil executable initializes empty repositories, opens native checkouts and has three delta file diagnostics. The prepared source also has a glob diagnostic, with a focused source checkpoint. This source checkout also has explicit add and tracked status, plus scope selection and private recording and complete recorded ancestry. gos is an alias for gossil, and v is an alias for vcs. The issue group, or i, recognises each Gest command. This build runs issue init, issue task create, issue task list and issue task show, and refuses the others. Each diagnostic runs without a repository. Run it from this source checkout with just gossil, which builds and runs the executable through Cargo. Cargo may print build messages on stderr. Command Arguments Successful output vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA Writes DELTA; no stdout vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Writes TARGET; no stdout vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Prints ok and a newline vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... Prints SQL, patterns and match indices; prepared source just gossil vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA just gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET just gossil vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Replace capitalized arguments with file paths. The commands accept exactly the number of paths shown. Each diagnostic requires the vcs or v group. The help section says how to list the commands. File data comes from paths and goes to paths. Stdin and stdout do not carry it.

title: CLI reference
text: Both executables print help. The help lists the groups and commands that this build runs. It also names the planned groups, and marks them as not available. Command Output gossil, gossil --help, gossil -h, gossil help Product help: the groups and the commands of vcs and issue gossil vcs, gossil vcs --help, gossil vcs -h, gossil vcs help Help of the vcs group gossil vcs COMMAND --help, gossil vcs COMMAND -h Usage of one command gossil vcs help COMMAND, gossil help vcs COMMAND The same usage of one command gossil issue, gossil issue --help, gossil issue -h, gossil issue help, gossil help issue Help of the issue group gossil issue task create --help, gossil issue help task create Usage of one issue command Each form works with gos in place of gossil, v in place of vcs and i in place of issue. Help goes to stdout, and the executable exits with status 0. A help request reads and writes no file. The product help also names the planned groups ui (u) and serve (s). This build does not run them. Before a group or a command name, --help, -h and help mean the same. Several of them in a row count as one. So gossil help help prints the product help, and gossil vcs --help open and gossil vcs help help open print the usage of open. init, new, info, timeline, log and verify print their own help, which the sections below describe. So do issue init, issue task create, issue task list and issue task show. Every other command prints its usage line and one sentence about what it does. After a vcs command, only a lone --help or -h asks for help. The issue section gives the rule after an issue command. With more arguments, the command parses --help by its own grammar, so vcs init -- --help creates a file named --help. The word help after a command is an ordinary argument, so vcs init help creates a repository named help. An unknown name fails with status 2 and two lines on stderr. The second line points to the help: gossil: unknown command "frob" Run "gossil --help" to list the commands. An unknown command after vcs gives gossil: unknown vcs command "NAME", then Run "gossil vcs --help" to list the vcs commands. A planned group gives gossil: the group "NAME" is planned and not available in this build. The issue section gives the errors of the issue group. A diagnostic without its group, such as gossil test-delta-apply, is an unknown command too. A help request with an argument after the command name, such as vcs help open extra or help vcs open status, fails with status 2. The first line on stderr is then Usage: gossil vcs help COMMAND.

title: CLI reference
text: The issue group, or i, recognises every Gest command that the Gossil CLI specification lists (CLI-02). The top-level commands are artifact, config, generate, init, iteration, migrate, project, purge, search, self-update, tag, task, undo and version, with their subcommands. They keep the aliases of the Gest source: a, i, p, t and u stand for artifact, iteration, project, task and undo. grep stands for search. new, rm, ls, view and edit stand for create, delete, list, show and update. Under iteration, rm stands for remove. delete stands for unset under meta. Help shows the aliases that Gest shows, and hides a, i, t, u, grep and delete under meta, as Gest does. This build runs init, task create, task list and task show, which the sections below describe. The issue guide runs them in one session beside check-ins. The build recognises each other command and refuses it: $ gos i task claim lkpunroy gossil: issue task claim is not available in this build The refused command then exits with status 69, the code of an invalid state. It reads and writes no file, and it does not open or create a database. The parser checks the command names only. Arguments after the last name, such as lkpunroy, are not checked. A --help or -h among the arguments prints the help of the command. So does a cluster of short flags that reaches h, such as -ah after task list. Each letter before h must be a flag of the command that takes no value, and no letter can come twice. Only v can come twice, because Clap counts it. So -vvh asks for help, and -aah and -jjh do not. As in Clap, an option that takes a value reads the rest of the cluster as its value, so -sh gives the status h. Only init, task create, task list and task show read such clusters. After each other command, only --help and -h print its help. Clap also rejects a letter that repeats a flag of an earlier argument, but this build checks each argument on its own. So Gest exits with 2 on task list -a -ah, and this build prints the help. After --, --help and -h are ordinary arguments, so the build refuses gos i task claim -- -h like any other claim. Input Status Message on stderr A recognised command that this build does not run, such as i undo or i t claim 69 gossil: issue PATH is not available in this build artifact, config, generate, iteration, task or a note group without a subcommand 2 gossil: issue PATH needs a command An unknown name, such as i frob or i task frob 2 gossil: unknown issue command "NAME" i serve or i s 2 The unknown-name message, because the root groups ui and serve replace Gest’s server command A help request with an argument after a command that has no subcommands, such as i help task create x 2 Usage: gossil issue help COMMAND PATH is the canonical command path, such as task create, even when the user typed an alias. In the unknown-name message, NAME starts with the canonical path of its group, so i t frob gives "task frob". Each status 2 message has a second line that points to the help. Gest runs project, tag and each meta without a subcommand, so each of them gives status 69 when it stands alone. A name after one of them that is not its subcommand is an argument, so i p frob also gives status 69. A help request reads that name as a command name, not an argument, so i help p frob and i help t meta ID give status 2 with the unknown-name message. A --help or -h right after project, tag or meta also makes the next name a command name. Then i p --help frob and i t meta -h ID give status 2 too. After the argument, as in i p frob --help, the --help prints the help of the command. This build does not yet recognise the global options -v, --no-color and --no-pager, or --version at the group root. Before a command name, they fail as unknown names. init accepts the first three after its name, as the next section says. task list and task show accept --no-color and --no-pager after their names, and refuse -v with status 69.

title: CLI reference
section: Create the Gest project of a checkout
text: gos i init, or gossil issue init, creates the Gest project of the open checkout that holds the current directory. It stores the project as a private project ticket, and it binds the checkout to that project. A project ticket is the Fossil ticket that holds one Gest project, as the issue ticket guide says. All four forms of executable and group run the same command. First, make the checkout with vcs init and vcs open --root. Then run init in the checkout root or in a folder below it: $ cd /home/alice/project $ gos v init /home/alice/project.fossil $ gos v open --repository /home/alice/project.fossil --checkout work --root /home/alice/project Opened checkout work at /home/alice/project (repository fc0dd44fb5dcb4aaecff68e771149f0698cbec87, head 397b39fc09ae52025628af5f7fbddefae0bbf53301664e2965cc279e89141c4f) $ gos i init ✓ initialized project lkpunroy root /home/alice/project The short ID is the first 8 letters of the Gest ID of the project. The line root names the checkout root. Gest prints the current directory there, and Gossil prints the checkout root. The output has no color. init takes no repository or checkout selection. It finds the nearest .gossil marker at or above the current directory, and reads the locator that vcs open published. The locator selects the repository and the checkout. The command then admits them with the same rules as vcs open, configuration included. It never creates a repository, a checkout registration or a locator. In one transaction, init writes these rows: the rows of a private project ticket, as the issue ticket guide lists them one g_project_binding row, with the checkout ID, the Gest ID and the checkout root one g_checkout_project row, with the checkout ID and the Gest ID The ticket ID is 40 random hexadecimal digits, and the Gest ID is random. The date and both timestamps hold the current time. The user is the local login, the first nonempty value of GOSSIL_USER, USER, LOGNAME and USERNAME, or else root. A failure before the commit leaves every byte of the repository unchanged. A second init, or an init in a folder below the root, prints the same message for the bound project. It changes no byte. Gest also keeps the project that it finds. After init, every vcs command still works, and init works both before and after the first commit. init accepts --local, --no-color, --no-pager and -v, -vv or --verbose, and ignores each of them. The locator already selects the repository, so --local changes nothing. Every other argument fails with status 2: gossil: unexpected argument "--json" for issue init Usage: gossil issue init [OPTIONS] A lone --help or -h prints the help of init. The other exit statuses follow CLI-05, the list of exit codes in the Gossil CLI specification: Case Status Message on stderr Success, also for a checkout with a bound project 0 None An argument that init does not take 2 gossil: unexpected argument "X" for issue init No marker, a marker without a locator, or a repository without vcs open 78 gossil: no open checkout holds this directory; run gos v init and gos v open first A malformed locator 78 The locator error A configured data directory that conflicts with the locator, or that holds no gossil.db 78 configured storage conflicts with explicit repository A repository at an older catalog, or one that lost its Gossil tables 78 The message of the exit section A local login that is not UTF-8 78 gossil: the local login is not UTF-8; set GOSSIL_USER A failure of storage or admission, for example a changed binding row 74 The storage error, such as unsupported project binding state A repository that already holds a project ticket, while the checkout has no project 74 The refusal below A missing repository file, or another I/O failure 74 The I/O error A failed write of the success message to stdout, after the commit 74 gossil: issue init kept the project, and stdout failed: ERROR For a repository that already holds a project, the storage error holds this text: issue init needs one project creation, a registered checkout with no bound project, and a repository with no project; binding an existing project is not available in this build This build has these limits: The project is private only. init writes no audit row and no undo history. A text field cannot hold [. init writes no selectors, tags or links. init does not bind a project that the repository already holds. Gest binds the one live project, or refuses several of them as ambiguous. Gossil refuses both cases with status 74. Repositories of older Gossil versions are not supported.

title: CLI reference
text: gos i task create TITLE, or gossil issue task create TITLE, stores one private task in the Gest project of the open checkout. Run gos i init first. All four forms of executable and group run the same command. The aliases new and t work as in Gest, so gos i t new TITLE is the same command too: $ gos i task create "Write the docs" -p high -m area=docs ✓ created task nwlkpqzs title Write the docs The short ID is the first 8 letters of the Gest ID of the task. The output has no color. The text form follows the success message of the pinned Gest source, and its exact bytes are provisional. With -q or --quiet, the command prints the short ID alone. With -j or --json, the command prints the task as Gest’s JSON envelope. The envelope has the fields assigned_to, created_at, description, id, metadata, priority, project_id, resolved_at, status, title and updated_at, and then notes, relationships and tags. The last three are empty lists. The JSON status of a task in progress is inprogress, as in Gest. With both --json and --quiet, the command prints the JSON. Like init, the command finds the repository and the checkout through the locator of the nearest .gossil marker. It takes the project from the checkout binding that init wrote. In one transaction, it writes the rows of one private task ticket, as the issue ticket guide lists them. The ticket ID is 40 random hexadecimal digits, and the Gest ID is random. The date and both timestamps hold the current time. The user is the local login, as for init. A failure before the commit leaves every byte of the repository unchanged. The command accepts these options of Gest: Option Value -d, --description The description. Without it, the description is empty. -p, --priority 0 to 4, or critical, high, medium, low or lowest in any case -s, --status open, in-progress, in_progress, inprogress, done or cancelled, in any case. The default is open. done and cancelled also set resolved_at to the creation time. -m, --metadata KEY=VALUE, repeatable. A dotted key makes nested objects. true, false and numbers become JSON values, and other values become strings. --metadata-json A JSON object, repeatable, merged key by key after the -m pairs -j, --json and -q, --quiet The output forms above -r, --raw, --no-color, --no-pager, -v, --verbose Accepted, and they change nothing The parser follows the rules of Clap, the Rust parser of arguments that the Gest source uses. A short option can take its value in the same word, as in -p1, and a long option after =, as in --priority=1. Short flags can share one word, as in -jq. A word after -- is the title, even when it starts with -. A -h inside a word of short flags, as in -jh, prints the help, by the rule of the issue section. The help options differ from Clap in two cases. Clap refuses -d -h T, because -d has no value. This build prints the help. Clap also refuses -j -jh T, because -j comes twice. This build prints the help, because it checks each word on its own. The command refuses these inputs: Input Status Message on stderr An unknown option, a second title, a repeated option other than -m, --metadata-json, --tag, -l, --link and -v, or a word that is not UTF-8 2 gossil: issue task create: PROBLEM, then the usage line A missing value, or a separate value that starts with -, such as -p -1 2 gossil: issue task create: "--priority" needs a value A priority or status that Gest does not accept, such as -p 5 or -s closed 2 gossil: issue task create: invalid value for "--priority": ... --phase without --iteration 2 gossil: issue task create: "--phase" needs "--iteration" --assign, --batch, -i or --iteration, -l or --link, --phase or --tag 69 gossil: issue task create: --assign is not available in this build No title 69 gossil: issue task create: reading the title from stdin is not available in this build; give TITLE A -m pair without =, a key of more than 32 parts, or --metadata-json that is not a JSON object 64 The Gest message, such as gossil: issue task create: --metadata-json must be a JSON object A [ in the title, the description or the metadata, including a JSON array 64 gossil: issue task create: the title contains "[", ... A task artifact of more than 65,536 bytes 64 gossil: issue task create: the task has at least N bytes, more than the 65536 that this build stores No open checkout 78 gossil: no open checkout holds this directory; run gos v init and gos v open first A repository at an older catalog, or one that lost its Gossil tables 78 The message of the exit section A checkout with no project 78 gossil: this checkout has no Gest project; run gos i init first A local login that is not UTF-8 78 gossil: the local login is not UTF-8; set GOSSIL_USER A failure of storage or admission, or another I/O failure 74 The storage or I/O error A failure of the JSON output, after the commit 65 gossil: issue task create kept the task, and JSON output failed: ERROR A failed write to stdout, after the commit 74 gossil: issue task create kept the task, and stdout failed: ERROR The command checks the usage errors first, then the refused options, then the title. It then opens the repository and checks the project. The checks of the metadata, of [ and of the size of the artifact come last. Gest uses another order, and checks the project first, before the title and the metadata. The command never reads stdin and never opens an editor. Gest reads the title or the description from stdin or from $EDITOR when they are missing. This build refuses a missing title and stores an empty description. Each command checks what it reads and writes in its own transaction. So a command sees each commit that another command made after the open, and needs no second open for it. A command can wait for the write lock longer than its timeout and refuse with database is locked. Every issue command takes that lock, the two read commands included. The refusal database is locked comes before the commit. init, task create, task list and task show then open the repository again and try once more. A second refusal gives 74, so many commands at once can still fail. This build has these limits: The command stores private tasks only. The command writes no audit row and no undo history, so a task that this build creates cannot be undone. A text field cannot hold [, because Markdown backlinks are not ported. The command writes no tags, links, iteration membership or assignment. Repositories of older Gossil versions are not supported. A task artifact holds at most 65,536 bytes. A task needs a project that the repository holds and that is not archived. The cost of a write does not grow with the count of tasks. The issue ticket guide gives the measured times of each command at 100, 1,000 and 5,000 tasks. With many commands at the same time, a command can still refuse with 74 and database is locked after its one retry, and it stored nothing. When the write of the task waited too long, the message starts with gossil: issue task create:. When the opening of the repository waited too long, the message is the storage error alone, without that prefix.

title: CLI reference
section: List the tasks of the project
text: gos i task list, or gos i t ls, prints the tasks of the project that init bound to the open checkout. It finds the repository as init does, and it writes nothing. The newest task comes first, and the list leaves out each task that is done or cancelled: $ gos i task list lqrooooo in-progress P1 Task o lmommmmm open P1 Task m The text output is provisional, as the issue read guide says. --json prints the JSON of Gest. The guide gives the order, the filters and both forms of output. task list accepts these options: -a or --all adds the tasks that are done or cancelled. -s STATUS or --status STATUS keeps the tasks in that status. Without --all, a done or cancelled task stays out. -j or --json prints JSON. --no-color and --no-pager change nothing. The Gest pin is the Gest commit that this build follows. Its other options are --assigned-to, --limit, -t or --tag, -q or --quiet, -r or --raw, and -v or --verbose. The command exits with status 69 on each of them: gossil: issue task list option --limit is not available in this build

title: CLI reference
text: gos i task show ID, or gos i t view ID, prints one task. The ID can be the full 32-letter Gest ID or a prefix of it that names one task. The command searches the tasks of every project, as Gest does, but it still needs a bound project. It accepts -j or --json, --no-color and --no-pager. It refuses -q or --quiet, -r or --raw, and -v or --verbose with status 69. The issue read guide gives the search and the output. While other commands write, a read can wait too long for the lock, as a write can. Then task list and task show open the repository again and read once more. They print the output only after the read succeeds, so a second try does not print it twice. A second refusal gives 74. The two read commands exit with these statuses of CLI-05: Case Status Message on stderr Success 0 None A parser failure, such as an unknown option, an extra argument or no ID 2 gossil: and the problem, then the usage line An option that this build does not support 69 gossil: issue task COMMAND option --NAME is not available in this build, where COMMAND is list or show An invalid prefix, such as L 64 gossil: Id prefix must contain only characters k-z, found 'L' A prefix that names no task 66 gossil: not found: id prefix 'PREFIX' A prefix that names more than one task 66 gossil: ambiguous id prefix 'PREFIX': matches N entities No open checkout holds the directory 78 gossil: no open checkout holds this directory; run gos v init and gos v open first The checkout has no bound project 78 gossil: this checkout has no Gest project; run gos i init first A failure of storage or admission 74 The storage error A failed write to stdout 74 gossil: cannot write the output: ERROR The other failures of the locator and the configuration give the statuses that the init table lists. The parser checks the arguments before the command opens the repository. So a parser failure or an unsupported option exits with 2 or 69 even outside a checkout.

title: CLI reference
text: just gossil vcs init --admin-user alice --date-override '2026-11-18 12:34:56' NEW_REPOSITORY just gossil vcs new --sha1 ANOTHER_NEW_REPOSITORY Initialization accepts exactly one destination. Both executable names and both group names support init and its new alias. The destination must be new. The command refuses existing files, symlinks and SQLite recovery sidecars. Option Behavior --admin-user USERNAME, -A USERNAME Set the initial administrator --date-override DATETIME Set the root date; default now --sha1 Use SHA1 for the initial root and native hash policy --help, -h Print initialization help and exit successfully -- Treat following arguments as literal destination names Long value options also accept --name=value. Without an explicit administrator, the command selects the first nonempty value from GOSSIL_USER, USER, LOGNAME and USERNAME, in that order. If all are absent or empty, it uses root. No preference file is read or created. Administrator bytes reach native validation unchanged. The storage API requires valid UTF-8. Repository filenames retain native bytes, including names beginning with file:. Dates must be UTF-8 and accepted by the native date provider. The receipt prints the committed project and server identifiers, administrator and initial remote-access password. Keep that password private. A receipt write failure returns status 1 after commit and leaves the repository initialized. Other initialization failures also return status 1. Initialization help returns 0. The command creates an empty native root without a checkout. Templates, project display fields and global preference options are unsupported and rejected before creation. Use the separate open command below to register or reopen one empty-root checkout. The scope and commit commands below record private history. The bounded timeline and log commands below expose the recorded_timeline API. Revision selection and broader history commands remain deferred. An already installed mini-VCS preview has a separate command contract. This guide does not record a new installation or publication.

title: CLI reference
text: First registration binds one existing directory to the initial empty root. Reopen also admits the supported private history written by the library. The locator is an owner-local lookup file at ROOT/.gossil/checkout.json. Neither operation selects files, creates file history or restores working files. The source supports open and locator recovery. Installation and publication require separate delivery evidence. just gossil vcs open --repository PATH --checkout ID --root ROOT Option Behavior --repository PATH Required existing local repository database --checkout ID Required exact checkout ID, with UTF-8 text --root ROOT Existing directory for explicit first registration or same-root reopen Options take separate values and each may appear once, in any order. Unknown options, duplicate options, positional arguments and missing values fail. Open has no --register, --name=value or default repository selection. A lone --help or -h prints the usage of open, as the help section says. Use either gossil or gos, with either vcs or v. For first registration, create the repository separately with vcs init, then supply --root. Open requires an existing database and never creates one. The root can contain ordinary files and nested Git repositories. Their bytes remain unselected and unchanged. Native VCS open requires no issue, project or author initialization. It does not grant Gest project authority. The native library admits catalog6 with exactly zero or one registration, the supported tracking, scope and private recording history, and private issue tickets. Open checks only the facts whose cost does not grow with the history. gos v verify checks the whole history. Catalog1, unrelated file history and a second registration are outside this command. The command refuses a repository at an older Gossil catalog, 2, 4 or 5, before any effect, with exit 78. The storage guide defines those catalog formats. Native admission checks the repository and owner binding, canonical root, device/inode, registration and checkout keys. The locator cannot replace those checks. See native storage for identity, root and resource limits.

title: CLI reference
text: For an existing registration, omit --root and invoke open from its root or a nested directory: cd ROOT /path/to/gos v open --repository PATH --checkout ID Use an absolute database path when changing directories. Open searches from the canonical current directory toward the filesystem root and stops at the nearest .gossil marker. It does not skip an incomplete, unsafe or conflicting marker to select an ancestor. Explicit repository and checkout flags must agree with both the locator and admitted database registration. An explicit --root preserves that exact requested root. If discovery finds a marker at an ancestor, first registration refuses rather than reusing the ancestor checkout. Repeating open with the same root and an existing valid locator reuses the admitted registration and syncs the locator directory. If checkout.json is missing, rootless open can reconstruct it from the exact existing registration. When no marker exists, run from the registered root itself. Recovery authenticates exactly one matching registration and preserves its identities, native keys and registration count. It allocates no checkout and repairs no database state. An incomplete marker prevents a new registration through --root. Malformed or conflicting locators remain conflicts and are never replaced.

title: CLI reference
text: Open loads inherited Gest configuration from the invocation directory, even when --root names another directory. Explicit repository flags do not bypass configuration checks. Layers merge in this order, with later values taking precedence: The file named by GEST_CONFIG, or the platform configuration directory’s gest/config.toml when that variable is absent. Each ancestor from the filesystem root through the canonical invocation directory, reading .config/gest.toml then .gest.toml in each directory. Environment values with the GEST_ prefix. Double underscores separate nested keys, and key names become lowercase. A usable absolute storage.data_dir explicitly selects gossil.db inside that directory. Its canonical existing database must match --repository. A directory that holds no gossil.db conflicts too. The exact uppercase GEST_STORAGE__DATA_DIR accepts an absolute native-byte path without UTF-8 loss. An effective relative path is not an explicit selection and does not revive a value from an earlier configuration layer. Malformed TOML, unreadable configuration files and invalid table or value types fail before marker or database mutation. A configured database.url or database.host is unsupported and also fails, including with explicit CLI flags. These errors do not print the configured provider value. Typed I/O, TOML and JSON causes remain inspectable through the retained error chain. Configuration supplies no implicit database creation or fallback through an incomplete marker. The configuration adapter retains Gest’s MIT attribution at pinned source eaf821b19c3cf75b99d22e1cc70e0eff4a3562a8 in src/checkout_config.rs.

title: CLI reference
text: The locator contains exactly version, repository_path_hex, repository_id and checkout_id. Version is integer 1. The path is the actual absolute Unix database filename, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal without losing native bytes. The repository ID is the admitted 40-character lowercase identity. The checkout ID names the real persisted registration. Reading is bounded to 65536 bytes, including whitespace. Parsing rejects unknown or duplicate fields, trailing data and malformed versions, identities or path encodings. Decoded database paths are bounded to 16384 bytes and must be absolute and NUL-free. Locator checkout IDs are bounded to 8192 UTF-8 bytes. The native registration API separately requires its smaller 1024-byte ID limit. The marker and locator must belong to the effective user and must not be symlinks. A marker must be a directory without group or other write permission. A locator must be a regular file without group or other permissions. New marker directories use mode 0700, and new temporary files use mode 0600. Open refuses unsafe objects and preserves their bytes and permissions.

title: CLI reference
text: First registration prepares complete bounded locator bytes in an exclusively created temporary file inside the marker directory. It flushes and syncs that file before changing the database. After checked registration commit, it publishes through a hard link that cannot overwrite checkout.json, then syncs the marker directory. An identical existing locator also requires directory sync. There is no replacement or copy fallback when linking fails. Failure phase Preserved result and next action Preflight No new registration was committed by this locator attempt; resolve the input or namespace conflict CommittedUnpublished Registration remains committed; retry without --root from the registered root to reconstruct the missing locator DurabilityUnconfirmed Locator is present but directory durability is unconfirmed; preserve it and retry the same admitted open Published Locator is present and its directory was synced; owned temporary cleanup failed Cleanup targets only this attempt’s temporary pathname with its recorded identity. Unrelated crash leftovers and replacement objects are preserved. Callers must keep the namespace stable. The contract does not promise atomic filesystem/database commit or protection against hostile concurrent replacement. After all durable locator pins are lost, recovery cannot prove historical identity against malicious database substitution. Success prints Opened checkout ID at ROOT (repository REPOSITORY_ID, head HEAD) and returns status 0. HEAD is the shared head, which stays at the empty root when the library records private history. Failures return status 1 with a diagnostic on stderr. Locator diagnostics name their publication phase. Internal error categories do not change this process exit status. The one exception is a repository at an older Gossil catalog, which returns status 78, as Exit status and errors says. A receipt write failure can occur after successful publication. It preserves the committed registration and locator, so a failed command does not imply that nothing committed.

title: CLI reference
section: Add explicit paths and inspect pending additions
text: This source checkout provides vcs add and vcs status at the initial root or an admitted private recorded head. Add records tracking metadata. Status lists all tracked paths, their pending or recorded state, and their actual scope. Use the separate scope and commit commands below to select scopes and record files. First, use vcs open to publish or recover the locator. Then run these commands from the registered checkout root or one of its descendants: /path/to/gos v add --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --path notes/plan.md --path notes/review.md /path/to/gos v status --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work Both --repository and --checkout are required exactly once. Repeat --path PATH for each file. There are no positional path lists. Paths are exact UTF-8 names relative to the registered root, regardless of the invocation directory. Status accepts no paths. Neither command accepts --json, --root, scope switches or recursive selection. A lone --help or -h prints the usage of the command. Both executable names and both group aliases use this grammar. Add accepts existing regular files only. It rejects absolute paths, empty components, . and .., backslashes, duplicate paths within a batch, case aliases, symlinks and special files. On macOS, paths must also be ASCII. This implementation rejects non-ASCII paths because their filesystem name comparisons have not been qualified. The .gossil namespace, selected database, SQLite sidecars and known hard-link aliases are protected. Parent directories and leaves are opened without following symlinks, and their identities are rechecked before commit. Keep the filesystem namespace stable during the command. These checks do not promise protection against hostile concurrent replacement. The CLI bounds the complete tracked inventory and each batch to 4096 paths. Each path has at most 4096 bytes and 128 components. Add temporarily captures files to validate the batch. It limits those initial captures to 64 MiB of working bytes and uses a 64 KiB read buffer. The final recheck temporarily holds a second copy of one file alongside those captures, so captured bytes can total 128 MiB. These bounds exclude other process allocations. Native admission has separate finite bounds. If any bound is exceeded, the command returns an error. Add persists tracking metadata only. Earlier additions remain tracked across batches and reopen. A successful batch with new paths advances pending_version once. An existing-only batch validates and rereads its inputs without changing rows or counters. A failed batch rolls back its metadata changes. Working files are never written. Temporary reads do not create a stored content snapshot, a check-in or a recording receipt. Both commands print the complete tracked inventory in pathname order: Tracked paths (A: pending addition, R: recorded): A unselected "notes/plan.md" A unselected "notes/review.md" Each row starts with A for a pending addition or R for a recorded path. A tab separates the state, scope and path. Scope is unselected, shared or private. The path uses Rust debug-string syntax with quotes and escapes. A selected scope assigns a path to shared or owner-local private history. unselected means that no choice has been stored. Empty status prints only the heading. Status does not discover untracked files or report modified, missing, removed or renamed files. It does not reread working file content. An output failure returns status 1, and an add may already have committed. New paths have unselected scope. Add grants no recording or sync authority. The library API can persist explicit immutable scopes and record all tracked files when every scope is private. The scope and commit commands below use that API, including rereading files edited after add.

title: CLI reference
section: Select scopes and record private files
text: Run scope and commit from the registered root or a descendant. Both require --repository PATH and --checkout ID exactly once, plus a complete matching locator. Use vcs open first to publish or recover that locator. Neither command infers a repository, checkout or scope. The configuration, marker and identity checks described for open also apply.

title: CLI reference
text: /path/to/gos v scope --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --scope private --path notes/plan.md --path notes/review.md --scope shared|private is required exactly once. Supply at least one --path PATH; repeat that option for each exact tracked path relative to the registered root. The one chosen scope applies to every path in this request. Paths must already be tracked. Duplicate paths, conflicting choices and unsupported path spellings fail without persisting a partial batch. The choice is immutable. Repeating the same choice is a checked no-op, but changing it is refused. New choices advance the pending version once. A checkout can reopen with some scopes unselected or with both shared and private choices. Those states grant no recording or synchronization authority. Choosing shared scope prevents private recording of the complete tracked set. Shared recording and changing a persisted scope are not supported. Success prints Selected scopes: N followed by a newline. N is the number of requested paths, including choices already stored unchanged.

title: CLI reference
text: /path/to/gos v commit --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work --scope private --all-tracked --user alice --comment 'Save notes' --date-override '2026-11-21T12:00:00' Required option Meaning --scope private Explicit request for owner-local private recording --all-tracked Include the complete tracked set; no path subset is accepted --user ACTOR Explicit nonempty actor text, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes --comment TEXT Explicit nonempty comment, at most 1048576 UTF-8 bytes --date-override DATE Explicit native date text, at most 64 UTF-8 bytes Commit requires a nonempty tracked set with a stored private scope for every path. An unselected, shared or mixed set is refused before mutation. The command reads the complete tracked inventory and current checkout view. The library checks all seven view fields and reauthenticates owner, root, provider and scope. No caller-supplied replacement authority is accepted. Every commit rereads current bytes and executable modes. An edit needs no second add. Saving a file alone creates no history. Mode-only changes count as changes, but mtime-only changes do not. Working files remain unchanged. The first private check-in names the empty shared root as its parent. Later check-ins name both the previous private check-in and that shared root. The shared head stays unchanged. Dates must satisfy the native date grammar and be strictly later than every parent under native SQL date conversion. Actor, comment and date text must be UTF-8 without NUL. Comments containing [ are refused, including on a no-change request. This restriction narrows Fossil’s comment grammar. The command prints one of these lines, followed by a newline: Recorded private check-in: HASH No changes HASH is the new native check-in hash. An unchanged tree returns No changes without a new receipt or any changed head, counter, content or classification. A later add creates unselected paths again. Select their private scope before recording the expanded tree.

title: CLI reference
text: Both commands accept separate option values only. They reject positional arguments, unknown or duplicate options, --name=value, --root and --json. A lone --help or -h prints the usage of the command. Only --path may repeat, and only for scope selection. Commit accepts no --path, and scope accepts no recording metadata or --all-tracked. Both executable names and both group names use the same grammar. Checkout IDs are nonempty UTF-8, bounded to 1024 bytes. Scope selection and recording use the tracking limits above. These allow 4096 paths, 4096 bytes per path, 128 components, 64 MiB of retained working bytes and a 64 KiB read buffer. The temporary final file recheck can require another captured copy. Native content and parser limits also bound cumulative work across the complete operation. The library contract defines those budgets, immutable history checks, protected files and rollback guarantees. A capture, validation or transaction failure leaves no partial recording. An output failure returns status 1 and can occur after a durable scope change or private commit. A failed exit does not prove rollback. Reopen the same explicit binding and retry with unchanged files, valid metadata and a date later than the stored parents. After a durable commit, that retry prints No changes. Scope retries with the same choices preserve them unchanged.

title: CLI reference
text: The gos executable runs the same implementation as gossil. Both accept v as a short name for vcs. For example, this runs the same round-trip check: cargo run --locked --bin gos -- v test-delta FILE1 FILE2 Use either executable with either group name for initialization, native open, add/status, scope/commit, info, timeline/log, verify, the three delta diagnostics and the prepared glob diagnostic. Usage messages use fixed spellings regardless of the invocation alias. Add and status use gos v, and the other command usage messages use gossil vcs. The usage lines of the help all use gossil vcs.

title: CLI reference
text: Success and help return status 0. Usage, input, delta and output failures return status 1 with one diagnostic line on stderr. A recognised issue command that this build does not run returns status 69, as the issue section says. issue init returns the statuses of CLI-05, such as 78 and 74, and so do issue task create, issue task list and issue task show. An unknown group or command returns status 2, as the help section says. A help request with an argument after the command name also returns status 2, with two lines on stderr. A repository whose catalog marker names an older Gossil catalog, 2, 4 or 5, returns status 78 before any effect. The three lines on stderr name the repository, the catalog found and catalog6, and say to create a new repository with gos v init. The CAT-07 message of the specification also names gos i init. In this build gos i init makes no repository, so the message leaves it out. The catalog marker is the storage_version value of the g_storage table, and not the .gossil checkout marker. Open, verify and every command that reads a repository check the catalog marker before they set any SQLite pragma that writes to the file. So a plain SQLite file, a stock Fossil repository or a file at an older catalog keeps every byte, and its header too. A stock fossil rebuild drops every table that Fossil does not know, so it drops each g_ table. A repository that holds Fossil tables but no Gossil tables returns status 78 before any effect, with this message: this repository has lost its Gossil tables (was `fossil rebuild` run on it?); restore it from a backup Missing input reports no such file: PATH. An output-open failure reports unable to open file "PATH" for writing. Invalid delta application reports Delta application failed.. A failed round trip reports delta test failed. Create and apply read their inputs before opening the output. This permits an output path to name an input file. Input or validation failures preserve an existing output, but an output write failure can leave it truncated. Parent folders must already exist. The encoder guide and decoder guide describe format bounds and the library errors behind these diagnostics. The getting started example uses distinct output files.

title: CLI reference
text: gossil-conformance is a separate development executable. It runs one explicit inherited-test configuration through just conformance CONFIG. It does not implement a Gossil engine. Its configuration, prerequisites and acceptance rules are in the runner guide.

title: CLI reference
text: Run info from the registered root or a descendant with a complete checkout locator: /path/to/gossil vcs info --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work /path/to/gos v info --repository /absolute/history.gossil --checkout work Both executable names accept both vcs and v. Repository and checkout selections are required exactly once. The command accepts no revision argument, hash prefix, tag, --root or --json. Standalone --help or -h succeeds without reading a checkout. Success prints exactly five lines in this order: repository: "/absolute/history.gossil" local-root: "/absolute/work" checkout: FULL_CURRENT_NATIVE_ID shared-head: FULL_SHARED_NATIVE_ID private-head: FULL_PRIVATE_NATIVE_ID_OR_none Each line has one ASCII space after the colon and ends with LF, including the last line. Both paths are standard JSON strings with escaping for special characters. repository preserves the supplied UTF-8 spelling, including relative paths and symlink aliases, after successful admission. Non-UTF-8 repository input is rejected without lossy conversion. local-root is the authenticated canonical registered root. All heads are complete native IDs. checkout is the private combined head when present, otherwise the shared head. Before the first private recording, private-head is the literal none. The shared head stays at the initial public check-in after private recordings. Uncommitted edits do not change these recorded identities. Info authenticates the existing checkout before producing stdout. Wrong selections, missing or incomplete nearest locators, configuration conflicts and corrupted native state fail through the existing admission checks. Errors retain their underlying causes. Success and failure preserve repository logical state, locator bytes and working files. Database file bytes can change during provider admission. An output failure returns status 1 and can leave partial stdout. This command adapts Fossil’s current-tree checkout identity assertion from test/set-manifest.test:68-73 and the current-checkout branch of src/info.c. Fossil prints a 40-character checkout prefix, and its same_uuid helper accepts matching prefixes. The inherited test is copyright 2016 D. Richard Hipp under the Simplified BSD License. Gossil controls compare complete output IDs against an independently authenticated checkout view. This bounded subset does not implement Fossil’s full info interface, general timeline filters, parent traversal or historical revision selection. Unrelated inherited suites are outside this qualification.

title: CLI reference
text: Broader version-control commands are planned. Neither gossil nor gos accepts them, and each fails with status 2, as the help section says. This build recognises the Gest commands other than init, task create, task list and task show, and refuses them with status 69, as the issue section says. The short names above apply to initialization and the three delta diagnostics, the prepared glob diagnostic, native open, add/status, scope/commit, info, timeline/log and verify. Shared recording, changing scopes, removal, rename, materialization, sync and Gest record associations remain unsupported.

title: CLI reference
text: Run from the registered checkout root or a descendant after vcs open has published a complete matching locator: just gossil vcs timeline --repository REPO --checkout ID just gossil v log --checkout ID --repository REPO Replace REPO and ID with the existing database and exact checkout identity. Both selectors are required, each once, with separate values in either order. Repository text is bounded to 4096 UTF-8 bytes and checkout text to 1024 bytes. Empty values, NUL, invalid UTF-8, duplicate or unknown options, positional arguments and --name=value forms fail. There are no filters, revision selectors, --limit or --json options. Output is always complete newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), with one object per line. The eight forms are gossil vcs timeline, gossil vcs log, gossil v timeline, gossil v log, gos vcs timeline, gos vcs log, gos v timeline and gos v log. They emit identical bytes for the same admitted history. Standalone --help or -h after either command prints usage and exits 0 without opening storage. Help combined with selectors fails. Each compact JSON object has the keys hash, date, actor, comment and private, in exactly that order. The first four values are strings, and private is a boolean. Every object ends with one LF, with no optional whitespace. Hashes are full native identities. Strict UTF-8 conversion and standard JSON escaping preserve the exact native date and decoded actor and comment, without normalization or date reformatting. The current check-in comes first and the immutable shared root occurs exactly once, last. Only the root has private: false. Before private recording, the root is the sole row. Opening uses existing-locator admission and publishes or repairs no locator. The API then walks every manifest of the chain in its own transaction. It refuses an event whose user or comment is not the U or C card of its manifest, and a chain whose length differs from the generation. Neither operation reads working-file contents. Pending additions and dirty or deleted working files do not change the recorded output. Missing checkout, corrupt or unsupported state and exhausted bounds fail without a partial history. Opening admission, the API operation and serialization each have a separate finite allowance. They do not form one aggregate budget for the whole invocation. The API operation parses every manifest of the chain under one parser ledger of 4,096 cards. A check-in of one file has about 8 cards, so timeline and log refuse a chain of about 500 such check-ins with exit 1 and recording native artifact validation. status, commit and gos v verify still admit that repository. Earlier releases had the same bound. For serialization, N counts the UTF-8 source bytes of all four string values, including each hash once. The checked worst-case bound adds 6*N to the exact syntax overhead. That overhead is 61 bytes per private row or 62 per root row and includes keys, quotes, punctuation, boolean and LF. The cumulative bound must fit the CLI decoded-content limit and the platform allocation limit. The adapter reserves space once before serializing the complete response. The API records its result and completes its checked transaction before the adapter prepares output. Stdout receives no bytes until complete preflight and serialization succeed. Success exits 0. Failures exit 1 with a diagnostic and retain the original cause. A repository at an older Gossil catalog exits 78. A stdout write failure can leave partial stdout. The read preserves logical database state and working files. This contract makes no claim that physical database bytes remain identical. See qualification before treating this source command as released or installed. General Fossil timeline behavior and cat remain separate work.

title: CLI reference
text: Run the full proof of a repository, or the proof of one issue: gos v verify --repository REPO gos v verify --repository REPO --issue ID The command takes --repository once and --issue at most once, in either order. Each value must be UTF-8 text of 1 to 4096 bytes, without NUL. Any other value gives the exit status 1. The four forms gossil vcs verify, gossil v verify, gos vcs verify and gos v verify all run it. A lone --help or -h prints the usage line Usage: gossil vcs verify --repository REPO [--issue ID]. The command changes no byte of the repository. Without --issue, the command replays every check-in and every issue artifact. It compares each native and typed table with that replay. Open and the other commands do not. They check only the facts that each one reads, as check a repository says. On success the command prints one line and exits 0: verified: 1 check-ins, 4 issues, 15 tables compared The first count gives the private check-ins and the second the task and project creations. The third count gives the table comparisons that passed. Each comparison covers a whole table, so the third count does not grow with each new issue or check-in. --issue ID takes a Gest ID or a prefix of one. Unlike issue task show, it does not prefer open tasks. The prefix must match exactly one task or project in the combined scope, whatever its status. The command proves one task or project from its own rows. The command replays the one artifact of the issue and compares its event, tagxref, ticket, ticketchng and typed rows with that replay. It replays no other artifact. For a task, it checks only that a typed project row with its project ID exists. On success it prints verified issue ID: ticket K and exits 0, where K is the ticket ID. --issue checks only a subset of the repository. It proves the rows that belong to the issue and that an index reaches. The rows are its artifact, ticket, change row, event, tag, tag row, private mark, typed row and, for a task, its project. It does not claim that no other row in the repository names the issue. Only gos v verify without --issue makes that claim. The proof of one issue reads its rows by an index or a primary key. The one exception is a scan of the ticket table to find the ticket of the ID. The proof also checks that each table that the full proof keeps empty in every repository has no row, with one fixed query per table. A repository with no checkout must also keep unsent, filename, mlink, plink, g_path_scope, g_project_binding and g_checkout_project empty. Only the full proof checks those seven whole tables. The proof of one issue does not see a row that no index of the issue reaches, or a typed row in another scope. The full proof refuses those rows. The proof of one issue refuses a task whose project the repository does not hold, which the full proof admits. See the proof of one issue. The statuses follow CLI-05. A failed proof prints on stderr the fixed refusal of the first check that fails, such as stored issue rows differ from the ticket artifact. The command then exits with 74, the status of a database value that is not valid. An invalid prefix exits with 64. A prefix that names no issue, or more than one, exits with 66, with the messages of issue task show. A usage error or a failed write to stdout exits with 1. A repository at an older Gossil catalog exits with 78. The proof bounds each artifact and each row by the limits of the CLI. Only timeline and log set a bound on the whole history, as the section on them says. The time of the full proof grows with the count of issues and check-ins. A stock fossil rebuild drops the Gossil tables, and then the command exits with 78, as every command does.

title: CLI reference
text: The source accepts all four forms: gossil vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gossil v test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gos vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... gos v test-glob PATTERN STRING ... Supply one pattern-list argument and at least one candidate argument. Arguments are positional. There are no switches, settings lookup or JSON mode. A token such as --help is a literal pattern or candidate when arity is valid. A lone --help or -h after test-glob prints its usage. A pattern list beginning with @ fails with test-glob setting lookup is not implemented. Missing arguments fail with Usage: gossil vcs test-glob PATTERN STRING ... for every alias. For PATTERN equal to *.rs,src/* and candidates src/lib.rs and notes.md, the source-defined output is: SQL expression: (x GLOB '*.rs' OR x GLOB 'src/*') pattern[0] = [*.rs] pattern[1] = [src/*] 1 1 src/lib.rs 0 0 notes.md Pattern labels start at zero. Match indices start at one, and zero means no match. Each candidate row prints reusable then one-shot results, followed by the original candidate bytes and LF. Pattern and candidate bytes are not escaped. The diagnostic constructs SQL with trusted expression x but executes no SQL. The adapter caps list and candidate inputs at 1 MiB each, pattern count at 65,536 and SQL output at 16 MiB. These bounds do not limit engine matching time or stack use. Unix arguments preserve raw bytes. Other platforms accept Unicode as UTF-8 and reject unrepresentable arguments with test-glob argument is not valid Unicode. Success exits 0. Usage, settings, encoding, budget, allocation and stdout errors exit 1. Budget messages use glob NAME limit exceeded, and capacity overflow uses glob capacity overflow. Allocation messages begin glob allocation:. Stdout failures print unable to open file " " for writing, preserve the original I/O cause and may leave partial stdout. The command reads no repository, settings or files and changes no tracking state. The glob guide defines quotes, first-NUL truncation and the SQL parser’s extra advance after closing quotes. Historical controls used 0.9.30. The 2026-11-21 focused checkpoint exercised all four forms with the libSQL 0.10.0 engine. Complete frozen-tree and delivery qualification are separate. These source forms make no claim about installed previews.

title: CLI reference
text: Use the three diagnostics for file deltas. For a native checkout, initialize a new repository, then register one explicit existing root with open. Next, reopen without --root, add explicit files, select private scope and commit all tracked paths. Use info to inspect the recorded checkout identity. Follow the source walkthrough and preserve durable state when a command reports an output failure.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Gossil is designed to keep agent files, typed issues and their connections to code in one coordinated history alongside Git. A historical view selects an exact file head, complete issue and discussion boundaries, and versioned links between issues and code. Git remains the source-code authority. This page compares that intended design with Git’s available behavior. The source CLI initializes empty repositories without a checkout, registers or reopens one native checkout and offers three delta diagnostics. It also supports explicit add and status without recording file content. Status distinguishes pending and recorded paths and shows their actual scope. The Rust library has typed converters for Gest tasks, projects, authors, artifacts, iterations, tags, notes, relationships, entity tags and iteration tasks. It also has a task artifact emitter and native storage primitives. It stores and reads private task and project tickets, as the issue ticket guide says. Native checkout open registers or reopens an existing directory and publishes its lookup locator. The library can record the complete private tracked tree. The source scope and commit commands expose that operation with explicit selections and metadata. The issue group recognises the names of the Gest commands. It runs gos i init, which creates the Gest project of an open checkout. It also runs gos i task create, which adds a private task to that project. gos i task list and gos i task show read its tasks. The other issue commands remain planned. See the current limits and CLI reference before trying a command.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: In Git, the working tree contains the files you edit. The index is the staging area for the next commit. Normally, a commit records the index as a file tree, with parents and a message. You can stage selected changes before committing; a commit need not include every edit on disk. See the Git tutorial and commit reference. Git can version task documents, plans and evidence in that same tree. Branches and commit history support many ways to organize the work. Git notes can attach information to an object without changing that object; notes have their own references and history. See Git notes. Need Git Intended Gossil design Record selected files Commits retain trees selected through the index or commit options Native file check-ins retain explicitly tracked agent files Record a task Version a task document or use a chosen tracker and integration Typed project/task records have defined fields, identities and reconstruction rules Select an earlier review state Name commits and any separately required task or notes history Select the file head plus complete exact boundaries for issues, links and discussions Connect an issue to code Adopt conventions or tools for references and reverse lookup Version typed links to registered Git repositories and support lookup in both directions Coordinate related changes A commit can include code and task documents in one tree One local database transaction coordinates selected Gossil files, records, scope and checkout heads Keep private agent material Choose a repository layout and sharing policy Keep private and shared material within one repository, with an explicit internal boundary A standalone tracker beside Git or Fossil can also retain detailed history. The extra requirement is to coordinate the exact states and dependencies that belong to a review. Gossil defines that coordination as part of its repository model, rather than leaving it to a convention between independent tools. Fossil already has immutable ticket artifacts and file history. The repository guide explains Gossil’s specified additions.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Suppose an agent revises plan.md, marks its task ready for review, and saves a private trace of a failed approach. The implementation is in a separate Git repository. In the planned Gossil workflow: Review the plan diff, task changes and permitted evidence together. Request the integrated operation with the expected file and issue revisions. Record the Gossil artifacts, derived records, scope, local command history and checkout heads in one database transaction. Retain the permitted file head and the complete issue boundaries for later review. A file head identifies a file check-in. An issue boundary identifies its scope, complete contributing artifact set and projection version. Artifacts are immutable stored records; the projection version names the rules that reconstruct the issue’s values. Contributors include losing assignments even when a current screen displays other values. Notes, links and discussions need their required dependencies too. If the agent later changes only the task’s status, the file head stays the same. The earlier issue boundary still selects the state reviewed with the plan. Record-only changes create no file check-in. Later arrivals do not silently change that selected historical set, subject to permission and byte availability. A file hash alone cannot recover this context. The code link names a registered Git repository, full commit, path and blob, with a versioned selector when it names a range. The blob identifies file bytes. From the issue, a reviewer can reach the pinned code; from that code version, the reviewer can find the issue. A known filename or current checkout path helps locate material, but neither supplies its repository identity or historical version. Local paths can change without changing the registered repository’s identity. The design introduces no global file identity. Uncommitted code needs a captured snapshot. An authorized capture can retain bytes if the external Git checkout later disappears; an object reference alone does not guarantee availability. The link descriptor encoding remains unfinished. See the repository guide for the planned coordination and its limits. The integrated transaction commits changes to the Gossil database. An external Git commit remains a separate operation. Checkout files are written after database commit through recoverable work, so filesystem recovery can still be necessary. Ordinary issue edits do not automatically batch unrelated work.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The planned Gossil checkout root can sit above several Git repositories. Select AGENTS.md and chosen agent files inside those repositories explicitly; initialization does not track every descendant. Gossil’s selection is independent of the nested Git indices and must preserve their branches and commits. The repository guide shows how to choose this layout. Git ignore rules help omit untracked files; they do not affect files already tracked. Sparse checkout controls which tracked paths appear in the working tree. Neither mechanism establishes a private/shared boundary for stored history. See gitignore and sparse checkout. Git transfer can select references through refspecs, which map source references to destinations. This selects history to fetch, not a confidentiality policy for individual paths. Access rules depend on the chosen repository and service configuration. See Git fetch. Gossil’s chosen design keeps private and shared history in one local repository. Shared history must be usable without private-only dependencies. Team replication, sync and autosync remain planned; this design does not promise arbitrary partial sharing within the shared portion today. This page follows the nossaifd writing guide, including principles credited to Rosalind Reid, Shreya Shankar and Oskar Austegard.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The private recorder saves a snapshot of every tracked file. Add enrolls paths rather than staging their bytes. The recorder reads those paths again, so it includes edits made without re-adding. Each path needs an explicit immutable private scope choice before recording. This operation creates owner-local file history and leaves the shared empty root unchanged. Shared recording and synchronization remain unsupported. The qualification record separates the checked library checkpoint from the CLI checkpoint still awaiting final gates.
