The installed tracking release, version 0.5.0, includes neither scope selection nor private recording. The source library also reads complete recorded ancestry through recorded_timeline. Its rows preserve full native hashes and exact metadata bytes, current first and shared root last. The source timeline and log commands print those rows as compact NDJSON with explicit selectors and an existing matching locator. This bounded reader does not establish general Fossil timeline compatibility.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: The glob source matches bounded Fossil pattern lists and constructs SQL expressions. It adds no ignore rules, filesystem traversal or wildcard selection to add or status. Its focused source checkpoint passed with the selected 0.10.0 engine. Complete frozen-tree and delivery qualification are separate.

title: Compare Gossil with Git
text: Keep Git for source work today. Next, try the delta tutorial and use the repository guide to select agent files. For a future integrated review, retain the exact file head, complete issue boundaries and versioned code links together.

title: Library concepts
text: Gossil separates byte operations, artifact structure and local database ownership. A byte operation does not create a repository, and a parsed artifact does not establish its place in a repository graph. For file selection, check-ins, branches and sharing, read working with repositories. This page describes the library modules available to application authors.

title: Library concepts
section: Files and issues in one operation
text: The intended product coordinates agent files and structured issue records in one repository database. A local operation can commit a plan revision, its task change and a private trace together. Its transaction includes canonical artifacts, derived projections, scope, local command history and Gossil checkout heads. A projection is stored state reconstructed from retained artifact records. Git remains the external source authority; its commits are separate operations. Checkout filesystem writes follow database commit through recoverable work. This integrated workflow remains planned. A historical view selects a permitted file check-in and exact record boundaries for each issue or discussion. The record boundary names the complete contributor set and projection version, with all dependencies required by the claimed view. Contributors are immutable artifacts that determine the record’s state. The projection version identifies the reconstruction rules; scope distinguishes shared access from an authorized owner’s combined view. Record-only changes create no file check-in, so a file hash alone cannot identify issue history. Later arrivals do not change the selected historical set. Access still depends on permission and byte availability. Typed links connect an issue to exact code versions and support reverse lookup from code to issues. A Git target pins its registered repository, commit, path and blob, with a versioned selector for a range. Captures can retain the permitted bytes; an object ID alone does not guarantee their availability. Shared history must be complete without private-only dependencies. Receiving it does not automatically update a checkout or an owner’s private issue selection. Explicit update and publication enforce the relevant revision and scope checks. A descriptor is a structured record naming a versioned link target and any selected range. Its transferable encoding remains unfinished, so these guides do not yet give a format that applications can exchange. Fossil supplies immutable file and ticket history; Gest supplies task workflows. Gossil’s specified additions coordinate exact issue boundaries with shared/private file heads and strengthen Gest’s multi-statement helpers with one owned transaction. Planned command undo validates complete inverse changes and rejects stale dependencies; it retains artifacts and does not rewind Git. Read compare Gossil with Git for the plan/task example and working with repositories for file selection. The library modules below form the implemented subset.

title: Library concepts
text: The delta module creates and applies Fossil deltas. Application takes an explicit output limit. The compression module packs and unpacks blobs, which are stored byte sequences. Unpacking also takes a decoded size limit. The content_hash module computes content digests. A digest identifies bytes but does not grant access to them. The artifact_checksum module computes legacy MD5 checksums for artifact records. It does not choose the repository’s content hash policy.

title: Library concepts
text: The token_codec module escapes byte values for Fossil record tokens. Its byte and C-string forms have different zero-byte behavior. The token guide defines those contracts. The artifact module parses eight structural artifact types with explicit limits and checks their structure and checksums. A caller implements DateProvider, whose julianday method converts date fields to Julian day numbers. Repository graph validation requires more storage rules. See the parser guide.

title: Library concepts
text: LocalStore owns a local libSQL connection and one exclusive write transaction. A transaction must commit or roll back before the connection returns to the store. The public interface does not expose arbitrary SQL. LocalOwnerRepository initializes a complete empty public root. Its initialize constructor creates a repository without a checkout. The vcs init command calls this constructor, generates identities and a password, and selects a default administrator from the environment. The API requires those values explicitly. Its create constructor creates catalog1 and binds an existing checkout directory. Catalog1 and catalog6 name storage formats; the native storage guide defines their creation and admission rules. After initialize, register_checkout can register one existing directory in catalog6. checkout_view authenticates its ID; checkout_view_for_root authenticates its exact root. These library methods change no working files and publish no locator. The source vcs open adapter adds locator publication and recovery around those admitted database operations. Open does not select additional files. Generic private content writes require the bound catalog1 repository and refuse catalog6. Catalog6 has a separate private recording API, described below. Its shared root stays a check-in with no files. Admission validates the stored root and authority before repository operations. For catalog6, open checks only the facts whose cost does not grow with the history. Each command then checks what it reads and writes, in its own transaction. gos v verify gives the full proof of the tracking, scope and private history state, and of each private issue ticket against its artifact. SharedView restricts access to public content that passed admission. Read and write access to the database file through the operating system establishes local owner authority. The native storage guide defines admission, content bounds and access rules. General links between artifacts in the repository graph remain planned, so parsing does not establish parent relationships or resolve references. Sync and team authentication also remain planned.

title: Library concepts
text: Gest is a task and artifact tracker. These converters use its record model for tasks, projects, authors, artifacts, iterations, tags, notes, relationships, entity tags and iteration tasks. The gest_task_values module validates eleven already decoded task fields. It returns an owned record with a standardized status and UTC timestamps. The task values guide defines validation and caller responsibilities. The gest_project_values module validates the four fields that make up the canonical Gest project record, gest_id, archived_at, created_at and updated_at. It returns an owned record with an identifier, nullable archive time and UTC timestamps. The project values guide defines the complete field contract. A local checkout root is outside the canonical project record. The gest_author_values module validates six canonical author fields and returns an owned record. It preserves names and nullable email exactly, normalizes author types and converts timestamps to UTC. The author values guide defines this conversion separately from native actors and local principals. The gest_artifact_values module validates eight canonical artifact fields and returns an owned record. A Gest artifact is a document such as a spec, not a Fossil artifact. The module keeps the title and body exactly, and it accepts a null or RFC3339 archive time. The artifact values guide defines the field contract. The gest_iteration_values module validates nine canonical iteration fields and returns an owned record with a lowercase status and UTC timestamps. A completed or cancelled iteration requires a completion time, and an active one requires null. The iteration values guide defines the field contract. The gest_tag_values module validates four canonical tag fields and returns an owned record. It keeps the label exactly as given, including its case, and converts timestamps to UTC. The caller checks that labels are unique across records. The tag values guide defines the field contract. The gest_note_values module validates seven canonical note fields. It keeps the body exactly as given, keeps a null author as null and returns the entity type in lowercase. The note values guide defines the field contract. The gest_relationship_values module validates eight canonical relationship fields. It returns the relationship type and both entity types in lowercase, and keeps the direction as given. The caller checks that each directed link is unique, and it checks the inverse row. The relationship values guide defines the field contract. The gest_entity_tag_values and gest_iteration_task_values modules validate the four canonical fields of each join record. A join record links two other records and has no Gest ID of its own. The entity tag converter returns the entity type in lowercase. The iteration task converter checks that the phase is an unsigned 32-bit integer. The caller builds the key tuple of each join record and owns each incarnation, which is the ticket of one attachment or membership. The entity tag values guide and the iteration task values guide define the field contracts. The gest_model module is a copy of the Gest record types and of their primitive values, such as Id and TaskStatus. The converters parse each identifier and each kind of status or type with these primitives, so the converters and the model accept the same text. A record that a converter has validated converts into its model record through the From trait. The Gest model guide describes the module. The task ticket emitter produces bounded creation artifact bytes from a validated task, a separate native ticket identity, actor bytes and a typed UTC date. The Gest ticket emitter takes the same inputs for a validated artifact or project, and the three kinds share one emitter. Before passing decoded values to a converter, callers must check raw field presence, duplicates and byte limits. The issue ticket writer stores a task or project creation privately. The command gos i init stores a project this way, and gos i task create stores a task. The commands gos i task list and gos i task show read the tasks. The other commands for these records remain separate work.

title: Library concepts
text: Tracking and scope are separate choices. add_files enrolls paths without staging their bytes. An absent scope row means unselected, not shared or private. select_path_scopes persists an immutable PathScope::Shared or PathScope::Private choice for an already tracked path. Repeating an equal choice is a checked no-op; changing a choice is unsupported. commit_private_tracked_files requires every tracked path to have private scope. The caller supplies the complete path set and the latest CheckoutView. The recorder captures current bytes and executable modes, so edits after add need no second add. It writes one complete private check-in and updates the combined head while leaving the empty shared head unchanged. The combined head selects the owner’s private tree together with the shared tree, which is empty in this supported recording family. The operation checks every field of the tracked rows, and checks its parent in full against the parent of that parent. So its cost does not grow with the history, and it never stores a check-in that gos v verify then refuses. A content budget bounds stored, decoded and retained bytes. A parser ledger counts input bytes, cards, owned bytes and entries across parsed artifacts. Both bound work across the checks, capture, construction and final validation. An unchanged tree returns NoChange without a new receipt or changed head or counter. Working files remain unchanged. Read native storage for request metadata and limits. Shared recording, synchronization and integrated issue operations remain planned. The source scope and commit commands use these library contracts. They require the complete locator binding and explicit repository, checkout and scope selections. Commit also requires all-tracked consent and explicit actor, comment and date. Final CLI qualification is still pending. The library reader recorded_timeline returns the complete current-first ancestry through the shared empty root. It walks every manifest of the chain, and checks the user and comment of each event against the U and C cards of its manifest, in the same transaction. It reads no working-file contents and returns no partial result when a bound fails. See the recorded ancestry contract. The source timeline and log commands print those rows as compact NDJSON after existing-locator admission and checked API completion. Opening, the API and serialization have separate finite bounds.

title: Library concepts
text: The prepared glob module parses Fossil pattern lists and calls the selected libSQL engine for matching. A result is the first matching one-based pattern index, or zero. Its finite limits bound bytes and pattern counts, not engine matching time or stack use. Matching selects no files and traverses no directories. glob_expr builds SQL from a trusted expression and escaped patterns. Bind untrusted candidate values through SQL parameters in a caller-owned connection; never put those bytes in the expression argument. The storage API still exposes no arbitrary SQL. The glob guide describes the distinct SQL parser advance and the current qualification limits.

title: Library concepts
text: Choose the smallest module that fits the operation. Next, set resource limits at every decoding or parsing boundary and read that module’s error contract.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: gossil-conformance executes one Fossil Tcl suite against an explicit program. It is development infrastructure and implements no Gossil engine behavior. A reference run tests the pinned upstream Fossil program. A candidate run tests the replacement program whose compatibility is under development. The runs have separate configurations and output directories. A missing candidate never falls back to C Fossil. Run just conformance-self-test to check the runner controls. These tests pass when the runner correctly rejects deliberate failures and incomplete runs. That result does not mean the inherited Fossil suites pass.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Install Rust with Cargo, Git, Just and uv on PATH before using the recipes. Rust builds the runner, Just runs Justfile recipes, and uv runs the installed workflow tools. just setup supplies the Linux reference tools and fetches Cargo dependencies. just install --check checks the saved workflow installation. The required references are Tcl 8.6.18 and Fossil 2.29 at revision 7e8ecf0ce4, with TLS and FUSE disabled. On Linux, just setup builds these tools from the archives pinned in evidence/reference-tools.json. It needs a C compiler, Make, zlib development headers and CA certificates. The Tcl installation retains its shell, shared library and core runtime scripts. Verified tools become available through ignored .jlog/bin links after the complete installation is published. Its receipt retains source identities, configure flags and binary hashes. Repeated setup checks and reuses that installation. Changed cache bytes and unknown tool paths fail without replacement. Worktrees can check and reuse shared managed references read-only when their source receipt, binary hashes and runtime observations match. On other hosts, setup checks and keeps the existing reference tools. Supply them before setup if they are absent. The current macOS tools remain the existing Tcl installation in Homebrew storage and the pinned local Fossil build. Setup does not adopt those external tools into its managed Linux installation. The read-only pull-request release check runs just setup before the full just check. Only a successful push to main can run its source-tag job. Local Linux native-tool controls and Python installer controls are separate from Rust coverage and the full Rust suite in CI. The bounded native setup receipt records the executed Linux scope.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Write a JSON configuration with absolute paths. The following example uses the checked-in positive control. Replace /path/to/gossil with the checkout path. The output directory must not exist. Save this example as CONFIG.json. { "role": "reference", "revision": "b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6", "tcl": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/tclsh", "driver": "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/controls/tester.tcl", "executable": "/path/to/gossil/.jlog/bin/fossil", "suite": "pass", "run_dir": "/path/to/gossil/target/conformance/example", "timeout_ms": 3000, "seed": 20261117, "inputs": [ "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/tester.tcl", "/path/to/gossil/tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch" ], "capabilities": {"tls": "disabled", "fuse": "disabled"} }

title: Inherited-test runner
text: Field Meaning and effect role Required label reference or candidate. It does not select a binary. revision Nonempty source identifier retained in evidence. The runner does not verify a source checkout against it. tcl Absolute path to an executable Tcl interpreter. driver Absolute path to the enabled tester.tcl driver. executable Absolute path to the program under test, used without fallback. suite Suite basename without a slash, for example pass for pass.test. run_dir Absolute path to a new output directory whose parent already exists. timeout_ms Positive deadline in milliseconds. A timeout rejects the run. seed Unsigned 32-bit value passed to Tcl srand before the driver runs. It controls Tcl randomness, not every source of randomness in the tested program. inputs Absolute paths to extra source, fixture or patch files whose bytes need hashing. capabilities Caller-supplied string map retained as evidence. It neither enables features nor verifies their availability. invocation_plan Optional complete plan and corpus pins; omitted or null uses strict duplicate-name rejection. See the plan contract below. The runner locates  .test beside driver. The example runs tests/fixtures/controls/pass.test. For an upstream suite, keep the original source tree and corpus unchanged. Put a copy of tester.tcl and the selected suite beside each other in a separate harness directory. Apply tests/fixtures/fossil/enable.patch only to the copied driver. Prepend set argv0 /absolute/path/to/original/test/tester.tcl to that enabled copy, using the original driver path in the pinned source tree. This restores the original corpus location when the driver derives testdir from argv0. Set driver to the enabled copy. The executed delta1 harness uses this layout; its original driver, suite and corpus bytes remain unchanged. The runner hashes the driver, suite, interpreter and tested executable automatically, in addition to every path in inputs. The example’s revision is the Git mirror commit for the inherited source. Fossil identifies the same source snapshot with its native revision, starting 7e8ecf0ce4. The full pair and driver hashes are in the repository file evidence/baselines/fossil/provenance.json. The label alone does not prove that an executable was built from that source. Create the parent output folder, then run just conformance CONFIG.json. Exit status 0 means this suite passed, status 1 means it failed acceptance, and status 2 means setup failed. The runner prints the report.json path. The report retains decoded stdout and stderr, commands, environment, hashes, source pin, suite, original assertion names, seed, capabilities and process status. The log files retain exact bytes and their hashes. Invalid UTF-8 blocks acceptance. Only stdout supplies assertion records, while stderr remains evidence. Without a plan, assertion identity combines the source pin, suite path and original name. The runner does not infer parameterized cases or unreported seeds. Callers must supply all fixture and source inputs that need hashing. Framework checks remain separate from real assertions. Known-bug annotations remain visible, but an assertion reported as failing never becomes a pass. Skipped summaries produce not-run with the original reason. The runner has no automatic feature-disabled mapping. A separate analysis must link the skipped reason to a capability observation, as the reference archive described in evidence/baselines/README.md does. The configuration map alone does not establish that classification. Timeouts and incomplete output produce blocked. Only pass contributes to acceptance. A skip or blocked result prevents acceptance of the entire suite, even if other assertions pass. A framework-only run fails acceptance. The runner also rejects missing summaries, inconsistent counts and crashes. For example, the final summary for one passing assertion is ***** Final results: 0 errors out of 1 tests. A final summary invalidates the run if a count is nonnumeric or exceeds the range of usize, Rust’s unsigned pointer-sized integer type. Every final-summary occurrence counts, including malformed ones. A duplicate summary or a later valid summary cannot clear that rejection.

title: Inherited-test runner
text: The default parser rejects repeated original assertion names. Some inherited suites reuse names for different source files. Such a run can opt into a complete, ordered plan of expected source-derived invocation identities. The plan preserves every original name, result, annotation and framework flag. Add an invocation_plan object to the configuration: { "invocation_plan": { "path": "/absolute/path/invocation-plan.json", "sha256": "EXPECTED_PLAN_SHA256", "expected_invocations": 22804, "corpus_manifest": "/absolute/path/corpus-manifest.json", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "EXPECTED_MANIFEST_SHA256", "corpus_root": "/absolute/path/upstream" } } expected_invocations pins the complete row count and must be positive. A count pin catches truncated plans during setup. It does not prove source correspondence. Both expected hashes must be lowercase SHA-256 values. The runner checks them before execution and parses those same verified bytes. The plan binds the configured suite, upstream revision, exact suite bytes and corpus manifest. The manifest binds every original corpus input. All physical paths are absolute. The runner assumes that no process changes input files during a run. This immutable-input assumption also applies to the existing input-hashing contract. Hash verification does not remove the race if another writer changes an input after verification. A plan uses schema gossil.invocation-plan.v1. Each row contains name and id. An ID contains suite and a structured position. Corpus positions use kind: "corpus", an upstream-relative source, a zero-based iteration and a positive slot. Empty controls use kind: "empty" with a positive index. The final framework position uses kind: "framework". For delta1, slot identifies one of the three assertions in each mutation iteration, numbered 1 through 3. The empty-control index identifies one of three final empty-input assertions, also numbered 1 through 3. The complete object shapes are shown below. These illustrative objects have one corpus row. They are not a complete plan for the real delta1 suite. Replace all hash placeholders with hashes of the exact bytes and include every real row. { "schema": "gossil.invocation-plan.v1", "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "suite_sha256": "SUITE_SHA256", "corpus_manifest_sha256": "MANIFEST_SHA256", "rows": [ {"name": "delta-example-0-1", "id": {"suite": "delta1", "position": { "kind": "corpus", "source": "test/example.txt", "iteration": 0, "slot": 1 }}} ] } The corresponding manifest has this shape: { "suite": "delta1", "revision": "PINNED_REVISION", "files": {"test/example.txt": "FILE_SHA256"} } Source paths use forward slashes and contain no empty, dot or parent components. IDs must be unique, and plan rows must cover every manifest source. Review of the generator and source establishes correspondence for every invocation. Hashes bind supplied bytes. Arbitrary identity labels alone do not prove provenance. The runner compares the entire observed vector with the complete expected original-name sequence and cardinality. It attaches expected_invocation_id only after an exact match. Invalid syntax remains malformed in either mode. No assertion is dropped, repaired, renamed or reordered. Failures, skipped summaries, bad totals, invalid UTF-8, nonzero exits and timeouts still reject. The report retains every plan row. The run directory also keeps exact verified invocation-plan.json and corpus-manifest.json bytes. Expected IDs describe correspondence derived from pinned source order. The original upstream log does not emit these IDs. Matching names cannot detect permutations or substitutions of whole groups with identical printed names. The frozen suite and original corpus establish their expected order. For the pinned delta1 corpus, generate the plan from the original source tree: just delta1-plan /absolute/path/fossil /absolute/path/new-plan-directory The generator uses the selected Tcl interpreter’s actual lsort order and file root behavior. lsort determines the order of corpus paths. file root removes the final filename extension to form the printed name stem. It preserves all non-directory corpus inputs and emits all 22,804 rows for 76 files, three empty controls and the framework assertion. The output directory must not exist. The source root must contain the original test/delta1.test and adjacent corpus. The recipe uses .jlog/bin/tclsh and labels the plan with revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. title: Inherited-test runner
text: The runner implements Unix process groups. The current checks ran on macOS, while Linux execution remains unqualified. Each invocation uses a fresh directory, a cleared environment, isolated HOME and temporary paths, and a fixed system utility PATH of /usr/bin:/bin. The runner observes completion without reaping the process-group leader. It checks the group identity before terminating owned descendants, then reaps the direct child. A timeout always rejects the run. Execution assumes trusted local programs with the same user credentials. The runner rejects setuid and setgid targets. Descendants that change their credentials, process group or session are unsupported. The runner is not a sandbox and does not promise a deadline for uninterruptible kernel work. It reaps its direct child and terminates descendants in the same process group. On macOS, XNU returns EPERM for a group containing only zombies. After the leader exits, the runner records that outcome as no-signalable-members under the trusted-program assumptions above. Other permission failures block the run. The XNU signal implementation defines that behavior.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: API: apply gives the exact contract. gossil::delta applies Fossil deltas to byte slices. A delta describes output with literal bytes and copies from an original byte slice. The library validates the commands before allocating output, then returns the decoded bytes. The gossil vcs test-delta-apply diagnostic exposes that decoder through files. It opens no repository or database and does not forward work to C Fossil.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: From the repository root, run: cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Replace ORIGIN, DELTA and TARGET with file paths. Quote paths that contain spaces. The command reads both inputs and finishes decoding before it opens TARGET. The target can be the same path as either input. On success, it writes exactly the decoded bytes, returns status 0 and leaves stdout and stderr empty. Cargo may print build messages on stderr before the executable runs. The command returns status 1 for usage, read, decode, allocation or write errors. The characterized diagnostics are: Failure Stderr line Wrong argument count Usage: gossil vcs test-delta-apply ORIGIN DELTA TARGET Missing input no such file: PATH Delta rejection or buffer reservation failure Delta application failed. Target open or write failure unable to open file "PATH" for writing Each diagnostic ends with one LF byte, and stdout remains empty. Other input read errors include the path and the underlying I/O error. The command has no root-level test-delta-apply alias. Usage, input-read and decode failures preserve an existing target because it has not been opened. A write failure can leave a truncated or partially written target. The command does not replace files atomically.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: The decoder API exposes output_size, apply, Limits and DeltaError. The same module also exposes the encoder function create. output_size(delta) parses only the advertised output size and its LF delimiter. It does not validate the commands or enforce the output limit used by apply. use gossil::delta::{Limits, apply, output_size}; let delta = b"3\n3:ABC0;"; assert_eq!(output_size(delta).unwrap(), 3); let output = apply(b"", delta, Limits { max_output_bytes: 1024 }).unwrap(); assert_eq!(output, b"ABC"); apply(source, delta, limits) returns Result , DeltaError>. The result has exactly the advertised size, with no trailing NUL byte. Both input slices must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The output ceiling is the smaller of limits.max_output_bytes and i32::MAX. Limits::default() uses i32::MAX, as does the file diagnostic. The first pass checks command syntax, source ranges, literal lengths, cumulative output length and the final size. After validation, the decoder reserves output storage with a fallible operation and replays the checked slices in a second pass. It stores no list of parsed operations. Invalid commands reach no output reservation. An empty result needs no reservation. The decoder returns these DeltaError variants: Error variant Meaning MissingHeaderNewline Header digits are not followed by LF. InputTooLarge A source or delta input exceeds the signed-length envelope. OutputTooLarge The advertised output exceeds the effective ceiling. TruncatedCommand A numeric command has no following operator. MissingCopyComma A copy offset has no present comma delimiter. UnknownOperator An operator byte is not defined. SourceRange A copy exceeds the source, including a zero copy beyond its end. OutputRange A command would exceed the advertised output. TruncatedLiteral A literal has fewer bytes than its count. Unterminated The input ends or reaches a command-start NUL before a semicolon. SizeMismatch A semicolon arrives before the advertised output is complete. AllocationFailed Output reservation failed, with the original TryReserveError retained as its cause. Fallible reservation reports recoverable allocation failures. It does not guarantee recovery from an operating-system kill or memory exhaustion after a successful reservation.

title: Bounded delta decoder
text: A delta starts with the encoded output length and LF. The form COUNT:BYTES inserts a literal, COUNT@OFFSET, copies from the source, and CHECKSUM; ends the delta. All numbers use the alphabet below. The decoder uses the exact unsigned-byte digit alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz~ Numbers wrap modulo 2^32, and empty numeric fields mean zero. High-bit bytes are not aliases for ASCII digits or delimiters. Zero-count copies still require a valid source offset and a comma. Literal payloads can contain arbitrary bytes. The decoder requires a semicolon and an exact final output size, then ignores trailing bytes. Checksum verification is disabled, as it is in the pinned reference build. The numeric field before the semicolon is parsed but not checked against the output. Accepted wrong-checksum fixtures remain accepted. Checked ranges and slice access reject truncation at boundaries where the C implementation can read beyond its logical input. Those C pointer behaviors are not format guarantees.

title: Bounded delta encoder

It returns Result , DeltaError>. It opens no database and calls no C implementation. The decoder guide describes how to apply the result.

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: use gossil::delta::{Limits, apply, create}; let delta = create(b"before", b"after").unwrap(); let restored = apply(b"before", &delta, Limits { max_output_bytes: 1024 }).unwrap(); assert_eq!(restored, b"after");

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: From the repository root, replace the capitalized arguments with file paths: cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta-create ORIGIN TARGET DELTA cargo run --locked --bin gossil -- vcs test-delta FILE1 FILE2 test-delta-create reads both inputs before opening DELTA for writing. The output can share either input path. Success returns status 0 with empty stdout and stderr. test-delta creates and applies deltas in both directions, compares both results with the original bytes, and prints ok followed by LF. A failed comparison, creation or round-trip application returns status 1 with delta test failed on stderr. File-buffer reservation failures return Delta application failed.. Cargo may print build messages on stderr before the executable runs. The commands require exactly three and two paths, respectively. Usage errors return status 1 and the matching usage line. Missing inputs produce no such file: PATH. Output failures produce unable to open file "PATH" for writing. Each diagnostic ends with LF. Other read errors retain the path and underlying I/O error. Usage and input-read failures preserve an existing output. Writing can truncate an existing output before a later write fails. These diagnostics have no root command aliases. They read and write file data through paths. test-delta uses stdout only for its ok diagnostic. Reading file data from stdin, writing file data to stdout, automatic parent-folder creation and complete native I/O diagnostic parity are outside this qualification.

title: Bounded delta encoder
text: The encoder follows the pinned Fossil src/delta.c algorithm. It indexes source landmarks, scans target windows for matching source bytes, and emits copies when they cover their encoding overhead. Other bytes become literals. Its rolling hash uses sixteen signed bytes, matching the selected native build. Checksums sum unsigned big-endian four-byte words with wrapping arithmetic and right-zero padding for the last short word. Sources of at most sixteen bytes produce one literal, including a zero-length literal for an empty target. Longer sources omit that zero literal. The hash tables omit the last complete source block and visit newer landmarks first. Each target window examines at most 250 candidates. Backward extension stops before source offset zero. A match equal to its encoding overhead is accepted. Equal-length candidates retain the first visited match, and the first target window with a winning match emits it immediately. Both inputs must fit within i32::MAX bytes. The encoder counts integer digits with unsigned arithmetic. The native signed shift above 2^30 is undefined. Unsigned counting there is a safe Rust policy and does not promise giant-input native parity. Slice lengths and addresses remain bounded by existing inputs. Every output append reserves storage before extending the vector. Both hash tables also reserve before initialization. EncoderAllocationFailed records the buffer stage, requested element count and original TryReserveError cause. The source and target size checks reuse InputTooLarge. Tests exercise genuine capacity-overflow errors without asking the allocator for giant storage. Fallible reservation does not promise recovery from an operating-system kill.

title: Compare normalized byte lines
text: The diff module compares two byte slices and returns an edit script in line counts. Use line_diff(from, to, options, limits) when a caller needs Fossil’s line matching and edit ordering without a rendered patch. Bytes need not be valid UTF-8. The module opens no files or databases. Normalize the input before calling this API. Fossil’s full text_diff wrapper uses blob_to_utf8_no_bom to remove a byte order mark or convert UTF-16. This module does neither. It also supplies no token diff, regular expression filter or text renderer. Its results describe the supplied bytes, after the caller’s chosen conversion.

title: Compare normalized byte lines
text: line_diff returns Result , DiffError>. Each Edit has three counts: Field Lines consumed copy Common lines from both inputs. delete Lines from FROM only. insert Lines from TO only. Read each triple in that order. Advance FROM by copy + delete and TO by copy + insert. The vector ends with the native zero triple, whose three counts are zero. Inserted content comes from TO. The script holds counts and omits line bytes. LF separates lines and is excluded from comparison. An unterminated final line still counts as a line. Adding or removing its final LF alone produces no line change. An empty input has zero lines.

title: Compare normalized byte lines
text: LineDiffOptions::default() selects exact comparison, native readability optimization and no other option. Choose these fields for each call: Field Behavior whitespace: Whitespace::Exact Compare all bytes within a line. whitespace: Whitespace::IgnoreEol Ignore trailing Fossil whitespace bytes. whitespace: Whitespace::IgnoreAll Ignore Fossil whitespace throughout a line. strip_cr Remove a trailing CR from each line before comparison. invert Exchange FROM and TO before computing edits. optimize Apply native readability shifts to insertions and deletions. not_too_big Reject more than 10,000 inserted plus deleted lines. Fossil whitespace here means bytes 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 32. It is not Unicode whitespace. IgnoreEol and IgnoreAll return the error DiffError::WhitespaceOnly when the script has one copy-only triple followed by the zero triple. They can also return scripts that contain edits.

title: Compare normalized byte lines
text: DiffLimits::default() supplies finite bounds. Applications can choose smaller bounds for their inputs: Field Default and meaning max_input_bytes 16 MiB combined input bytes. max_lines 200,000 combined input lines. max_edits 200,001 triples, including the final zero triple. max_work 100,000,000 charged inspections, comparisons and search iterations. The implementation also caps combined bytes at i32::MAX and combined lines at 1,000,000, even when caller limits are larger. Work is a charged algorithm budget. It does not measure each processor instruction or total heap bytes. Input bounds are checked before line-table allocation, and reservations can fail. DiffError::Binary reports an embedded NUL or a line longer than 32,767 bytes. WhitespaceOnly reports the rejection described above for the whitespace modes. TooManyChanges reports the enabled change-count rejection. Limit reports a caller bound or fixed cap, checked arithmetic failure or allocation failure. A failure returns no partial script.

title: Compare normalized byte lines
text: The algorithm derives from Fossil src/diff.c at revision b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6. The source correspondence record is evidence/diff/source-map.json. The raw fixture at tests/fixtures/diff/native-raw.json records reference identity and cases. The module retains its upstream copyright and 2-Clause BSD attribution. Bounded ordinary qualification passed all eight focused test groups and 143 native comparisons. The qualified src/diff.rs SHA256 is 0d7ce1bacd07ff2b922821ccfdb35e837f741a026dcce1e956917789c8bfa843. The exact freeze and receipt are retained in /tmp/gossil-fossil-diff-qualification-20261119/corrected-freeze.json and /tmp/gossil-fossil-diff-qualification-20261119/focused-receipt.json. An independent source review covered that frozen implementation. Execution-pending notes in the earlier source map are historical. The qualification receipt records the later candidate run. The raw fixtures do not establish full diff.test inheritance or show that the normalization, token, rendering and filtering wrappers are complete. Normal coverage and full project gates are required in addition to these historical receipts. Internal hashes for line matching follow the inspected native signed-char and byte-order behavior. High-byte inputs on other architectures, including Linux arm64, still need platform qualification. No cross-platform native parity is claimed by the macOS run.

title: Rust library examples
text: These examples use the library in this checkout. The byte and glob examples operate without opening a database; the ancestry example uses an existing admitted repository. For full signatures and errors, browse the generated API reference.

title: Rust library examples
text: Keep a source checkout of Gossil and add these sections to your application’s root Cargo.toml. Replace /absolute/path/to/gossil with that checkout’s path: [dependencies] gossil = { path = "/absolute/path/to/gossil" } serde_json = "1" [patch.crates-io] libsql = { git = "https://github.com/rahuldave/gossil-libsql", rev = "c02db34ae8a7e91ca7ab8faee18fe41515626940" } libsql-ffi = { path = "/absolute/path/to/gossil/vendor/libsql-ffi" } Cargo does not inherit patches from dependencies. The application must select both the corrected Rust wrapper and Gossil’s bundled libSQL provider itself. This provider preserves the Fossil date arithmetic used by artifact parsing and repository admission. The registry provider alone does not establish that compatibility. Preserve the bundled source and its provenance record. The wrapper guide describes the exact TEXT behavior and source checks. For a Cargo workspace, put both patches in the workspace root manifest. Save a complete byte-operation example below as src/main.rs inside fn main() { ... }, then run cargo run. The asynchronous storage example uses a separate runtime.

title: Rust library examples
text: use gossil::delta::{Limits, apply, create}; let origin = b"before"; let target = b"after"; let delta = create(origin, target).unwrap(); let restored = apply(origin, &delta, Limits { max_output_bytes: 1024 }).unwrap(); assert_eq!(restored, target); The limit caps decoded output. Handle DeltaError rather than unwrapping results in an application. The delta guides describe the format and validation bounds.

title: Rust library examples
section: Pack bytes and compute a digest
text: use gossil::{compression, content_hash}; let packed = compression::pack(b"abc", -1).unwrap(); assert_eq!(compression::unpack(&packed, 3).unwrap(), compression::Unpacked::Bytes(b"abc".to_vec())); assert_eq!(content_hash::sha1(b"abc").len(), 20); The compression level -1 selects the default. The unpack limit is three bytes. See byte primitives for empty inputs and digest choices.

title: Rust library examples
text: use gossil::token_codec::{fossilize, defossilize}; let escaped = fossilize(b"two words").unwrap(); let decoded = defossilize(&escaped).unwrap(); assert_eq!(decoded.bytes, b"two words"); Token escaping preserves the byte form described in the token guide. Use the explicit C-string function when zero-byte truncation is required. For asynchronous storage examples, see local storage. The artifact parser guide shows the date-provider boundary.

title: Rust library examples
text: Use an existing LocalOwnerRepository and explicit finite AdmissionLimits. This helper propagates StorageError and returns every supported ancestor: use gossil::storage::{AdmissionLimits, LocalOwnerRepository, RecordedCheckin, StorageError}; async fn recorded_history( owner: &mut LocalOwnerRepository, limits: AdmissionLimits, ) -> Result , StorageError> { owner.recorded_timeline("work", limits).await } Replace work with an existing checkout ID. Rows preserve native date, actor and comment bytes, and full verified hashes. The current check-in comes first; the shared empty root comes last. The shared empty root alone is a valid result before private recording. A missing checkout or exhausted bound returns an error rather than an empty or truncated history. See native storage for admission, transaction and ownership limits. To read the same ancestry from the source CLI, use timeline or log with explicit repository and checkout selectors and an existing matching locator. The CLI preserves metadata as JSON strings; the API fields remain byte vectors.

title: Rust library examples
text: This prepared source example uses explicit limits and preserves the first-match index. It requires the same provider patches shown above and fresh qualification of this adaptation. use gossil::glob::{glob_create, glob_expr, glob_multi_match, Limits}; let limits = Limits { list_bytes: 1024, candidate_bytes: 1024, patterns: 16, expression_bytes: 4096, }; let list = Some(b"*.rs,src/*".as_slice()); let patterns = glob_create(list, limits).unwrap(); assert_eq!(patterns.glob_match(b"src/lib.rs").unwrap(), 1); assert_eq!(glob_multi_match(list, b"notes.md", limits).unwrap(), 0); assert_eq!(glob_expr(b"?1", list, limits).unwrap(), b"(?1 GLOB '*.rs' OR ?1 GLOB 'src/*')"); Handle GlobError in an application. ?1 is a trusted parameter expression; bind the candidate separately when executing this SQL through your own database interface. glob_expr returns bytes and executes no SQL. It escapes only the patterns, so an untrusted expression argument can inject SQL. The glob guide defines NUL, quotes, SQL parsing and engine work limits.

title: Rust library examples
text: Start with in-memory byte operations. Next, handle typed errors and choose application limits before connecting these calls to stored or untrusted data.

title: Lexical file paths
text: The gossil::file_path module simplifies filename bytes by the rules of Fossil’s file_simplify_name function. Lexical simplification changes only the bytes of the name. It does not read the filesystem, resolve symlinks or make a name absolute. The native C source has one branch for Unix and one for Windows and Cygwin. The module ports both source branches, and the caller selects one of them on every host.

title: Lexical file paths
text: simplify_name(input, keep_trailing_slash, limits) uses the Unix branch and returns Result , PathError>. Give the complete filename as a byte slice, which does not have to be UTF-8. An empty input gives an empty output, and an input that contains a NUL byte is an error. use gossil::file_path::{Limits, simplify_name}; let limits = Limits { max_input_bytes: 128, max_output_bytes: 128 }; let path = simplify_name(b"a/b/../c/", false, limits).unwrap(); assert_eq!(path, b"a/c"); simplify_name_for_source(input, keep_trailing_slash, limits, platform) takes a SourcePlatform and returns Result . Source choice Behavior SourcePlatform::Unix Backslashes and extended prefixes stay ordinary bytes SourcePlatform::WindowsCygwin Backslashes become slashes, and the //?/ extended prefix is removed The source choice does not depend on the host operating system. A choice of WindowsCygwin does not show that Gossil runs correctly on Windows or Cygwin.

title: Lexical file paths
section: Read the result of a source branch
text: A SimplifiedName has two views of its bytes: reported_span() borrows the bytes that the native return value counts. visible_bytes() borrows the bytes before the first NUL, as a C string shows them. The two views differ for one input. For the Windows/Cygwin input //?/, native C copies the terminator of the input to byte zero but reports a length of one. So the reported span is [0], and the visible name is empty.

title: Lexical file paths
text: Limits has the fields max_input_bytes and max_output_bytes. The input must fit its limit. The module reserves one buffer of the input length plus one sentinel byte, the C terminator, before it copies the input. The output limit counts the reported span, and the span can hold an early NUL. So the input //?/ needs an output limit of at least one with WindowsCygwin, but its visible name is empty. Error Condition InputLimit The input exceeds its limit, or the buffer exceeds addressable memory OutputLimit The reported span exceeds its limit EmbeddedNul The input contains NUL TerminalCancellation A relative name cancels to before the start of the buffer Allocation The buffer reservation fails, and the error keeps the original cause

title: Lexical file paths
section: The order of the lexical rules
text: The module follows the loops of the native function in their order: With WindowsCygwin, it converts each backslash to a slash, then handles an initial //?/. If keep_trailing_slash is false, it trims the trailing slashes. It collapses duplicate slashes, but keeps an initial double slash. It removes leading ./, internal /./ and each /component/.. that can cancel. For example, //a stays //a, but // becomes / when keep_trailing_slash is false. Unresolved .. components stay, even above an absolute root. A nonempty name that simplifies to nothing becomes /. The trailing slash option does not keep every trailing slash. With the option true, a/// becomes a/, but a///./ becomes a. The second result comes from the collapse loop. The loop shortens the logical length but leaves the old bytes after it. A later /./ test can read those bytes, and the port keeps this behavior. With WindowsCygwin, the module compares the three bytes after //?/ with UNC, and it ignores ASCII case, as SQLite’s sqlite3_strnicmp does. A match gives an initial slash and skips UNC. So //?/UNC/a/b becomes //a/b. Without a match, the byte after the prefix moves to the start, and //?/a:/a/b becomes a:/a/b. The port does not check drives, the names after the UNC prefix or whether a name is valid.

title: Lexical file paths
section: When a relative name cancels past its start
text: A relative name such as a/.. cancels its last component back past the start of the name. The case is a relative terminal cancellation. Native backup_dir then leaves the output cursor at minus one, so native C writes the final terminator one byte before the buffer. The write is undefined behavior, and native Fossil has no defined result for these names. The port returns PathError::TerminalCancellation in place of a result. Examples are a/.., .../.. and a/../ with the trailing slash option false. The error is a safe policy of the port, and not a native result.

title: Lexical file paths
text: The port follows Fossil check-in 7e8ecf0ce4, the same check-in as the reference binary of the project. The source is src/file.c, lines 1172 to 1180 for backup_dir and lines 1195 to 1260 for file_simplify_name. The test test/file1.test and its BSD license text are copied unchanged into tests/fixtures/file-path/. The tests in tests/file_path.rs check these groups of cases: Group Source 25 cases of simplify-name 100 to 107 file1.test 6 cases of simplify-name 108 and 109 file1.test, which runs them only on Windows 14 Unix cases and 18 Windows/Cygwin cases adapter plans for a C copy of the native source Lexical controls, bounds and errors the Rust tests The test of the Windows/Cygwin plan also holds its own copy of the 18 cases. It compares the plan with that copy, so a dropped, added or changed case fails. An earlier run compiled the C copy on a macOS host, once for each branch. Each build passed all of its plan cases. The records of that run are not in the repository. The test-simplify-name command of the Fossil 2.29 binary gives the same output as the fixtures for all 25 inherited cases. It does the same for the Unix adapter cases with the option false. The command has no trailing slash option, so it cannot check the cases with the option true. Relative-name, relative-tree-name and absolute-tree-name operations are not part of the module, because they need a working directory and a repository root. The Windows and Cygwin branch has not run on a Windows or Cygwin host.

title: Lexical file paths
text: Select the source branch when a name needs platform conversion. Set byte limits, and keep reported spans apart from visible names. Apply the policy for the filesystem and for containment in a separate step. Next, qualify the Windows/Cygwin branch on a native host before code depends on it.

title: Gest artifact values
text: The gossil::gest_artifact_values module converts all eight canonical artifact fields into an owned, validated record. Use it for complete decoded snapshots before storage integration. Artifact persistence and CLI commands remain planned. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. A Gest artifact is a document with a title and a body, such as a spec or a plan. It is not a Fossil artifact. Here, canonical means the eight artifact fields in the reviewed field map. In a source checkout, the map is tests/fixtures/gest_artifact_values/source-map.json. ArtifactValueInputs requires an explicit serde_json::Value for gest_id, project_id, title, body, metadata, archived_at, created_at and updated_at. artifact_from_values returns an ArtifactValues record with private fields. artifact_to_values returns all eight fields as independent owned values. The upstream artifact model defines the source record. See library setup for Cargo dependencies.

title: Gest artifact values
text: Before constructing serde_json::Value inputs, callers check raw JSON for required fields, unknown fields and duplicate keys. Callers must check duplicate keys before decoding merges them. Then assemble every field for conversion. The archive time can be null, but the caller must give the null explicitly. The converter does not read a clock, generate an identifier, look up references or execute SQL. use gossil::gest_artifact_values::{ArtifactValueInputs, artifact_from_values, artifact_to_values}; use serde_json::json; let fields = ArtifactValueInputs { gest_id: json!("zyxwvutsrqponmlkzyxwvutsrqponmlk"), project_id: json!("kkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk"), title: json!(""), body: json!("Complete document body é"), metadata: json!([null, {"reviewed": false}]), archived_at: json!(null), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), updated_at: json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00Z"), }; let record = artifact_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let output = artifact_to_values(&record); assert_eq!(output.body, json!("Complete document body é")); assert_eq!(output.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(artifact_from_values(output).unwrap(), record); The example uses an empty title to show that strings have no content rule.

title: Gest artifact values
text: Both identifiers must contain exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. The title and the body accept any string, including an empty string, Unicode and null characters. Metadata accepts any JSON value, including null, scalars and arrays. The converter keeps the JSON value but not its raw spelling. Archive state accepts null or an RFC3339 timestamp. Creation and modification timestamps require strings. Shared validation uses chrono 0.4.44, normalizes to UTC and checks that the output can be parsed again. It imposes no time ordering. An archived artifact keeps its body. The archive timestamp does not mark the record as deleted. ArtifactValueError displays the field and a static reason without echoing input. Its parse_cause() accessor keeps the chrono error from input parsing or canonical UTC output parsing. Other failures have no parser cause. Callers own raw decoding, required-field presence, unknown-field classification, duplicate keys in the original input, byte budgets and reference checks. Callers also check the complete history of changes to the record. The converter does not check that the project exists. It does not implement lifecycle, replay, migration, storage or the complete Gest API.

title: Gest artifact values
text: The nine converter controls in tests/gest_artifact_values.rs check complete output, independent ownership, types, identifiers, metadata, archive state and timestamp boundaries with typed causes. One control checks that the source map names each field, and that it names only controls that exist in the file. The same control compares the map with the expected values in tests/support/gest_source_map.rs. These values are the Gest commit, the hash of each cited Gest file and the exact list of fields. They also include the hash of the test accounting addendum. The control then makes copies of the map, each with one stale or malformed entry, and checks that the comparison refuses each copy. The Gest files are not in this repository, so the control compares the hashes that the map records with these values. It does not hash the files themselves. These tests cover the converter itself. They do not reproduce the upstream artifact API or repository tests, whose behavior and persistence still need separate validation. Artifact storage and reads of caller-selected records remain planned through the repository transaction API. The Gest ticket emitter turns a validated record into bounded creation artifact bytes in memory.

title: Gest artifact values
text: Use the converter after checking the complete raw input. Next, adapt the example to your validated fields and use artifact_to_values to read the owned result.

title: Gest author values
text: The gossil::gest_author_values module validates all six canonical author fields in memory. Use it for complete decoded snapshots before storage integration. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. An author record identifies a human or agent in its record model. Accepting the human value here does not deliver native Human workflows. AuthorValueInputs requires an explicit serde_json::Value for gest_id, author_type, name, email, created_at and updated_at. author_from_values returns an AuthorValues record with private fields. author_to_values returns all six fields as independent owned values. See library setup for Cargo dependencies.

title: Gest author values
text: Before decoding raw input, check required fields, unknown fields and duplicate keys. Decoding can collapse duplicate keys. Then supply every field, including an explicit null for absent email. use gossil::gest_author_values::{AuthorValueInputs, author_from_values, author_to_values}; use serde_json::json; let author = author_from_values(AuthorValueInputs { gest_id: json!("kkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk"), author_type: json!("AGENT"), name: json!(" Alice "), email: json!(null), created_at: json!("2026-11-19T01:02:03.000000001+02:00"), updated_at: json!("2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"), }).unwrap(); let values = author_to_values(&author); assert_eq!(values.author_type, json!("agent")); assert_eq!(values.name, json!(" Alice ")); assert_eq!(values.email, json!(null)); assert_eq!(values.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T23:02:03.000000001+00:00")); assert_eq!(author_from_values(values).unwrap(), author); The modification time precedes creation in this example because conversion imposes no time ordering. It generates no identity or time and performs no SQL.

title: Gest author values
text: The identifier must contain exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. The author type accepts case-insensitive human or agent and emits lowercase. It rejects surrounding whitespace and other values. Names accept any string, including empty strings, whitespace and control characters. Email accepts an explicit null or any string. Null and an empty string remain distinct. Conversion does not check email syntax or trim either field. Both timestamps require strings that chrono 0.4.44 can parse as RFC3339. Conversion normalizes each instant to UTC and checks that its output can be parsed again. It rejects output outside that canonical RFC3339 domain. AuthorValueError displays the field and a static reason without echoing input. Its parse_cause() accessor returns the actual chrono error from input parsing or canonical output parsing. Other failures have no parser cause.

title: Gest author values
text: Callers own raw decoding, field admission, duplicate detection, byte limits, reference checks and the history of changes to the record. An author record is separate from native actor bytes and local principals. Conversion does not establish uniqueness, authorization, storage, lifecycle, replay, migration or the complete Gest API. The seven controls in tests/gest_author_values.rs cover field types, identifiers, author types, exact strings, nullable email, timestamps, parser causes and owned output. These controls exercise the pure converter. They do not test storage or native workflows. Their presence does not establish an executed test pass.

title: Gest entity tag values
text: The gossil::gest_entity_tag_values module converts all four canonical entity_tag fields into an owned, validated record. Use it for complete decoded snapshots before storage integration. Tag attachment and CLI commands remain planned. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. An entity_tag row attaches one Gest tag to one task, artifact or iteration. The row is a join record, which links two other records and has no Gest ID of its own. Here, canonical means the four entity_tag fields in the reviewed field map. In a source checkout, the map is tests/fixtures/gest_entity_tag_values/source-map.json. EntityTagValueInputs requires an explicit serde_json::Value for entity_id, entity_type, tag_id and created_at. entity_tag_from_values returns an EntityTagValues record with private fields, and entity_tag_to_values returns all four fields as independent owned values. The upstream entity_tag model defines the source record. See library setup for Cargo dependencies.

title: Gest entity tag values
text: Before you build the serde_json::Value inputs, check the raw JSON for required fields, unknown fields and duplicate keys. Check duplicate keys before decoding, because decoding merges them. Then assemble every field for conversion. The converter does not read a clock, generate an identifier, look up references or execute SQL. use gossil::gest_entity_tag_values::{ EntityTagValueInputs, entity_tag_from_values, entity_tag_to_values, }; use serde_json::json; let fields = EntityTagValueInputs { entity_id: json!("zyxwvutsrqponmlkzyxwvutsrqponmlk"), entity_type: json!("Artifact"), tag_id: json!("klmnopqrstuvwxyzklmnopqrstuvwxyz"), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), }; let record = entity_tag_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let output = entity_tag_to_values(&record); assert_eq!(output.entity_type, json!("artifact")); assert_eq!(output.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(entity_tag_from_values(output).unwrap(), record);

title: Gest entity tag values
text: The entity ID and the tag ID must each contain exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. The entity type accepts artifact, iteration and task. Gest ignores case when it parses an entity type, so the converter accepts Artifact and returns the lowercase spelling. A value with whitespace around it fails. The timestamp must be a string. The shared timestamp validation uses chrono 0.4.44. It converts the timestamp to UTC and checks that it can parse the output again. The Gossil contract gives each join record an immutable key, the JSON tuple [entity_type,entity_id,tag_id]. Each attachment of a tag also has its own ticket, called an incarnation. The tuple is stored in the field gossil_key when that ticket is created. At most one incarnation for a tuple may be live. The converter returns the three key fields with the entity type in lowercase. So two inputs that differ only in the case of the entity type give equal records. The converter does not build the key, choose the incarnation or check that only one is live. EntityTagValueError displays the field and a static reason, and does not repeat the input. Its parse_cause() accessor returns the chrono error from the parse of the input or from the parse of the canonical UTC output. Other failures have no parser cause. Callers own raw decoding, required-field presence, unknown-field classification, duplicate keys in the original input and byte budgets. Callers also own the key, the incarnation, the attachment and removal of a tag, and the check that the entity and the tag exist. The converter does not implement lifecycle, replay, migration, storage or the complete Gest API.

title: Gest entity tag values
text: The eight converter controls in tests/gest_entity_tag_values.rs check complete output, independent ownership, types, identifiers, entity-type spellings, the key fields and timestamp boundaries with typed causes. One of them checks that the source map names each field, and that each control that it names exists in the file. The same control compares the map with the expected values in tests/support/gest_source_map.rs. These values are the Gest commit, the hash of each cited Gest file and the exact list of fields. They also include the hash of the test accounting addendum. The control then makes copies of the map, each with one stale or malformed entry, and checks that the comparison refuses each copy. The Gest files are not in this repository, so the control compares the hashes that the map records with these values. It does not hash the files themselves. These tests cover the converter itself. They do not reproduce the tests of the upstream tag API or repository. The upstream EntityType enum has five tests of its Display and FromStr methods. The source map lists the five tests as later API obligations. The converter uses both methods through the port of EntityType in the Gest model, and the tests of that port run the five tests. The upstream constructor Model::new reads the clock and has no upstream test.

title: Gest iteration task values
text: The gossil::gest_iteration_task_values module converts all four canonical iteration_task fields into an owned, validated record. Use it for complete decoded snapshots before storage integration. Iteration membership commands remain planned. Gest is a task and artifact tracker. An iteration_task row places one task in one phase of one iteration. A phase is a number that orders the work inside an iteration. The row is a join record, which links two other records and has no Gest ID of its own. Here, canonical means the four iteration_task fields in the reviewed field map. In a source checkout, the map is tests/fixtures/gest_iteration_task_values/source-map.json. IterationTaskValueInputs requires an explicit serde_json::Value for iteration_id, task_id, phase and created_at. iteration_task_from_values returns an IterationTaskValues record with private fields, and iteration_task_to_values returns all four fields as independent owned values. Gest has no model file for this row, and the upstream iteration repository reads and writes it. See library setup for Cargo dependencies.

title: Gest iteration task values
text: Before you build the serde_json::Value inputs, check the raw JSON for required fields, unknown fields and duplicate keys. Check duplicate keys before decoding, because decoding merges them. Then assemble every field for conversion. The converter does not read a clock, generate an identifier, look up references or execute SQL. use gossil::gest_iteration_task_values::{ IterationTaskValueInputs, iteration_task_from_values, iteration_task_to_values, }; use serde_json::json; let fields = IterationTaskValueInputs { iteration_id: json!("klmnopqrstuvwxyzklmnopqrstuvwxyz"), task_id: json!("zyxwvutsrqponmlkzyxwvutsrqponmlk"), phase: json!(4294967295u32), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), }; let record = iteration_task_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let output = iteration_task_to_values(&record); assert_eq!(output.phase, json!(4294967295u32)); assert_eq!(output.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(iteration_task_from_values(output).unwrap(), record);

title: Gest iteration task values
text: The iteration ID and the task ID must each contain exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. The phase must be a JSON integer from 0 through 4294967295, the range of an unsigned 32-bit value. A negative integer, a larger integer, a float such as 1.0 and a string fail. Upstream, Gest stores the phase as an SQL integer and reads it back with a cast that wraps a value outside that range. The Gossil contract requires a checked range instead, so such a value fails. The timestamp must be a string. The shared timestamp validation uses chrono 0.4.44. It converts the timestamp to UTC and checks that it can parse the output again. The Gossil contract gives each join record an immutable key, the JSON tuple [iteration_id,task_id]. The phase is not part of the key. Each membership also has its own ticket, called an incarnation. The tuple is stored in the field gossil_key when that ticket is created. At most one incarnation for a tuple may be live. Gest adds a membership with INSERT OR IGNORE, so a repeated add keeps the existing phase. The converter does not build the key, choose the incarnation or apply that rule. IterationTaskValueError displays the field and a static reason, and does not repeat the input. Its parse_cause() accessor returns the chrono error from the parse of the input or from the parse of the canonical UTC output. Other failures have no parser cause. Callers own raw decoding, required-field presence, unknown-field classification, duplicate keys in the original input and byte budgets. Callers also own the key, the incarnation, the addition and removal of a membership, and the repeated-add rule. In addition, they own the check that the iteration and the task exist. The converter does not implement lifecycle, replay, migration, storage or the complete Gest API.

title: Gest iteration task values
text: The eight converter controls in tests/gest_iteration_task_values.rs check complete output, independent ownership, types, identifiers, the phase range, the key fields and timestamp boundaries with typed causes. One of them checks that the source map names each field, and that each control that it names exists in the file. The same control compares the map with the expected values in tests/support/gest_source_map.rs. These values are the Gest commit, the hash of each cited Gest file and the exact list of fields. They also include the hash of the test accounting addendum. The control then makes copies of the map, each with one stale or malformed entry, and checks that the comparison refuses each copy. The Gest files are not in this repository, so the control compares the hashes that the map records with these values. It does not hash the files themselves. These tests cover the converter itself. They do not reproduce the tests of the upstream iteration repository, which remain later obligations. The source map records the hash of the test accounting addendum, a review document. The addendum lists the upstream tests of enums and constructors that later API work must keep. It lists no such test for this row, so the source map lists no later obligation of that kind.

title: Gest iteration values
text: Before constructing serde_json::Value inputs, callers check raw JSON for required fields, unknown fields and duplicate keys. Callers must check duplicate keys before decoding merges them. Then assemble every field for conversion. An active iteration requires an explicit null completion time. The converter does not read a clock, generate an identifier, look up references or execute SQL. use gossil::gest_iteration_values::{IterationValueInputs, iteration_from_values, iteration_to_values}; use serde_json::json; let fields = IterationValueInputs { gest_id: json!("zyxwvutsrqponmlkzyxwvutsrqponmlk"), project_id: json!("kkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk"), title: json!("Sprint 4"), status: json!("COMPLETED"), description: json!(""), metadata: json!({}), completed_at: json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00Z"), created_at: json!("2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00"), updated_at: json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00Z"), }; let record = iteration_from_values(fields).unwrap(); let output = iteration_to_values(&record); assert_eq!(output.status, json!("completed")); assert_eq!(output.created_at, json!("2026-11-18T12:00:00+00:00")); assert_eq!(iteration_from_values(output).unwrap(), record); The example gives the status in capital letters to show that output uses the lowercase spelling.

title: Gest iteration values
text: Both identifiers must contain exactly 32 lowercase letters from k through z. The title and the description accept any string, including an empty string, Unicode and null characters. Metadata accepts any JSON value, including null, scalars and arrays. The converter keeps the JSON value but not its raw spelling. Status accepts active, completed or cancelled in any letter case, as the upstream parser does. Surrounding spaces and other spellings fail. A terminal status, which is completed or cancelled, requires an RFC3339 completion timestamp, and active requires null. The upstream row reader does not check this pair, but the Gossil contract requires it. The converter does not create a completion time. Creation and modification timestamps require strings. Shared validation uses chrono 0.4.44, normalizes to UTC and checks that the output can be parsed again. It imposes no time ordering. IterationValueError displays the field and a static reason without echoing input. Its parse_cause() accessor keeps the chrono error from input parsing or canonical UTC output parsing. Other failures have no parser cause. Callers own raw decoding, required-field presence, unknown-field classification, duplicate keys in the original input, byte budgets and reference checks. Callers also check the complete history of changes to the record. The converter does not check that the project exists. It does not implement task membership, lifecycle, replay, migration, storage or the complete Gest API.

The control then makes copies of the map, each with one stale or malformed entry, and checks that the comparison refuses each copy. The Gest files are not in this repository, so the control compares the hashes that the map records with these values. It does not hash the files themselves. These tests cover the converter itself, not the upstream iteration API or repository tests. The source map lists the six upstream tests of the status display and of the terminal check as later API work. The converter uses that display and that check through the port of IterationStatus in the Gest model. The tests of that port run the six tests.
