Field Type Description whitespace Whitespace Select exact, trailing-space or all-space comparison. strip_cr bool Remove a trailing carriage return, including on an unterminated line. invert bool Exchange FROM and TO before computing the script. optimize bool Apply native readability shifts (DIFF_NOOPT disables this). not_too_big bool Reject scripts with more than 10,000 inserted plus deleted lines. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default.

title: diff
text: source pub struct DiffLimits Caller-selected bounds on admitted input and algorithm work. Field Type Description max_input_bytes usize Maximum sum of the two input byte lengths. max_lines usize Maximum sum of the two input line counts. max_edits usize Maximum number of triples, including the terminating zero triple. max_work u64 Maximum charged byte inspections, comparisons and search iterations. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug, Default.

title: diff
text: source pub struct Edit One COPY/DELETE/INSERT triple, in numbers of lines. Field Type Description copy usize Common lines consumed from both inputs. delete usize Lines consumed only from FROM. insert usize Lines consumed only from TO. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq.

title: diff
text: source pub enum DiffError Native rejection or a caller resource boundary. Variant Description Binary Embedded NUL or a line longer than 32767 bytes. WhitespaceOnly Whitespace mode produced the native unchanged-script rejection. TooManyChanges not_too_big rejected more than 10,000 changed lines. Limit A caller bound, checked arithmetic or allocation failed. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq.

title: diff
text: source pub fn line_diff( from: &[u8], to: &[u8], options: LineDiffOptions, limits: DiffLimits, ) -> Result , DiffError> Compute native line COPY/DELETE/INSERT triples for normalized byte text. The result includes the native terminating zero triple. LF is excluded from comparison, so adding or removing the final LF does not change a line. This API does not perform the BOM or UTF-16 conversion of blob_to_utf8_no_bom.

title: diff
text: Returns DiffError::Binary for an embedded NUL or a line longer than 32,767 bytes. Returns DiffError::WhitespaceOnly when a whitespace mode produces one copy-only triple followed by the zero triple, and DiffError::TooManyChanges when not_too_big rejects more than 10,000 inserted plus deleted lines. Returns DiffError::Limit for caller bounds, fixed input caps, checked arithmetic or allocation failure. No partial script is returned on failure.

title: diff
text: use gossil::diff::{line_diff, DiffLimits, Edit, LineDiffOptions}; let edits = line_diff( b"old\n", b"new\n", LineDiffOptions::default(), DiffLimits::default(), ).unwrap(); assert_eq!(edits, vec![ Edit { copy: 0, delete: 1, insert: 1 }, Edit::default(), ]); Parameter Type Description from &[u8] Already-normalized FROM bytes. to &[u8] Already-normalized TO bytes. options LineDiffOptions Supported line comparison and edit options. limits DiffLimits Finite resource bounds for this invocation. returns Result , DiffError> Native triples ending in a zero triple.

title: file_path
text: The original code is copyright 2006 D. Richard Hipp, under the 2-Clause BSD license. The license text is in tests/fixtures/file-path/COPYRIGHT-BSD2.txt. The module ports the Unix branch and the Windows/Cygwin branch of file_simplify_name and backup_dir from Fossil check-in 7e8ecf0ce4. It does not read the filesystem, resolve symlinks, authorize paths or make names absolute. The tests of the source branches do not show that the code runs correctly on a native Windows or Cygwin host. No test has run on such a host. The input is a complete byte name with no NUL, and an empty input stays empty.

title: file_path
text: Set explicit limits for the application, and treat the result as lexical bytes. Next, apply the filesystem and containment policy of the caller in a separate step.

title: file_path
text: source pub struct Limits Limits holds the bounds of the caller on the input bytes and the returned bytes. Neither bound counts a C terminator. Field Type Description max_input_bytes usize Sets the largest number of input bytes that a call accepts. max_output_bytes usize Sets the largest number of bytes that a call returns. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug.

title: file_path
text: source pub enum SourcePlatform SourcePlatform names the branch of the native source to apply, whatever the host. Variant Description Unix Keeps backslashes and extended prefixes as ordinary bytes. WindowsCygwin Converts backslashes and removes extended prefixes, as native C does. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq.

title: file_path
text: source pub struct SimplifiedName SimplifiedName holds the span that the native code reports. The span can contain an early C terminator. Implements Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq.

title: file_path
text: source pub fn reported_span(&self) -> &[u8] Borrow exactly the bytes that the native return value counts. Parameter Type Description returns &[u8] The reported span. On Windows/Cygwin, the input //?/ gives the one-byte span [0].

title: file_path
text: source pub fn visible_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] Borrow the bytes of the diagnostic C string, which end before the first NUL. Parameter Type Description returns &[u8] The visible filename bytes, which can be shorter than Self::reported_span.

title: file_path
text: source pub enum PathError PathError reports a rejected input, an exceeded bound or a failed allocation. Variant Description InputLimit The input exceeds the bound of the caller or the largest buffer that memory can address. OutputLimit The simplified output exceeds the bound of the caller. EmbeddedNul The input contains a NUL, which has no accepted meaning in a filename. TerminalCancellation The native simplification would write its terminator before the start of the buffer. Allocation(TryReserveError) The reservation of the buffer failed before the input was copied. Implements Debug, Display, Error.

title: file_path
text: source pub fn simplify_name( input: &[u8], keep_trailing_slash: bool, limits: Limits, ) -> Result , PathError> Simplify a filename with no NUL by the Unix lexical rules of Fossil. Duplicate separators collapse to one, but an initial double slash stays. The function removes a leading ./, each internal /./ and each /component/.. that can cancel. Unresolved .. components stay, even above an absolute root. As in native Fossil, a nonempty name whose simplified bytes are empty becomes /. A relative name that cancels past its start, such as a/.., is a relative terminal cancellation. It leaves native C with a negative cursor and a terminator outside the buffer, and this function rejects it. The input buffer holds at most max_input_bytes plus one sentinel byte. The output bound applies to the actual length of the simplified name.

title: file_path
text: Returns PathError for an exceeded bound, a NUL, a failed allocation or a relative terminal cancellation.

title: file_path
text: use gossil::file_path::{Limits, simplify_name}; let bounds = Limits { max_input_bytes: 128, max_output_bytes: 128 }; assert_eq!(simplify_name(b"a/b/../c/", false, bounds).unwrap(), b"a/c"); Parameter Type Description input &[u8] The complete filename bytes, with no embedded NUL. keep_trailing_slash bool Keep a trailing separator where the native rules keep it. limits Limits The bounds of the caller on the input bytes and the output bytes. returns Result , PathError> The owned simplified bytes, without a terminating NUL.

title: file_path
text: source pub fn simplify_name_for_source( input: &[u8], keep_trailing_slash: bool, limits: Limits, platform: SourcePlatform, ) -> Result  Simplify a filename by the branch of the Fossil source that the caller selects. The Windows/Cygwin branch converts every backslash to a slash. Then it removes //?/ and compares the next three bytes with UNC, by the ASCII case map of SQLite. The function does not check drives, the names after the UNC prefix or whether a name is valid. For the input //?/, native C copies the terminator of the input to byte zero but reports a length of one. So the result keeps that NUL in its reported span, and its visible C string is empty. The input buffer holds at most the length of the input plus one sentinel byte. The output bound counts the reported span, with any NUL inside that span. After the loops compact the name, the native lookahead can still read the original bytes at the end of the buffer. A relative terminal cancellation returns the same error as simplify_name.

title: file_path
text: Returns PathError for an exceeded bound, a NUL, a failed allocation or a relative terminal cancellation.

title: file_path
text: use gossil::file_path::{Limits, SourcePlatform, simplify_name_for_source}; let bounds = Limits { max_input_bytes: 128, max_output_bytes: 128 }; let windows = SourcePlatform::WindowsCygwin; let unc = simplify_name_for_source(b"\\\\?\\UNC\\a\\b", false, bounds, windows).unwrap(); assert_eq!(unc.visible_bytes(), b"//a/b"); let prefix = simplify_name_for_source(b"//?/", false, bounds, windows).unwrap(); assert_eq!(prefix.reported_span(), b"\0"); assert!(prefix.visible_bytes().is_empty()); Parameter Type Description input &[u8] The complete filename bytes, with no NUL. keep_trailing_slash bool The native option to keep a trailing slash. limits Limits The bounds on the input and on the reported output span. platform SourcePlatform The source branch to apply, whatever the host. returns Result  The bytes that the native code reports, with a separate accessor for the visible C string.

title: gest_ticket
text: See the Gest ticket guide for the format, caller responsibilities and a library example. One shared emitter writes the creation artifact of every Gest kind. Each kind gives only its sorted field list and its gossil_kind value, so the task emitter in crate::task_ticket and the two emitters here write the same card syntax, size plan and checksum. The card order and the construction of tokens and the checksum follow Fossil tkt.c:1837-1874 (b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6). Fossil is Copyright D. Richard Hipp and contributors. Its BSD two-clause license is preserved in the frozen source evidence. This module performs no storage, identity generation or admission.

text: source pub fn artifact_creation_bytes( artifact: &ArtifactValues, ticket_id: &[u8], actor: &[u8], date: NativeDate, max_output: usize, ) -> Result , TicketError> Emit complete uncompressed Fossil ticket artifact bytes for a validated artifact creation. A Gest artifact is a document record, such as a spec or a plan. It is not a Fossil blob. The contract CHANGE-01 uses an artifact ticket as the carrier of a logical change. The ticket becomes a change only when a validated logical_change declaration is attached at its K. This emitter writes no declaration, and metadata alone never declares a change. The eight model fields are archived_at, body, created_at, gest_id, metadata, project_id, title and updated_at. Each uses JSON followed by native token escaping. The three fixed fields are gossil_deleted=false, raw gossil_kind=artifact and raw gossil_schema=1. The eleven J fields are sorted by name. The body keeps its exact text. A non-null archived_at does not mark the record as deleted. The K, U and D cards and max_output follow crate::task_ticket::task_creation_bytes.

title: git_reader
text: This module is the only place in Gossil that uses the gix crates. It opens one Git worktree and reads what binding needs, by GIT-01 of the Git access contract. Binding is the step that ties a Gossil change to a Git commit. The module reads the Git directory and the common directory, HEAD and a branch tip. It also reads a commit with its ordered parents, the object format and three configuration keys. The reader reads raw objects. It opens the object store with gix_odb::at_opts, with no replacement table and without multi-pack-index. So refs/replace never changes a result. It recomputes the hash of each commit that it reads, and it returns an error for a mismatch. Each read has a finite limit from Limits. The reader itself reads HEAD, each ref, a .git file, commondir, each configuration file and each alternates file. It reads each one without blocking and within its limit. It parses a loose ref, HEAD and packed-refs itself, as Git does, and gives the bytes of the configuration and of a .git file to the gix parsers. The reader refuses what the first release does not support, by GIT-04. It refuses a shallow clone, a reftable repository, an unknown object format, an unknown version-1 extension and a bare repository. It reads core.bare and core.worktree from the files that Git reads for the worktree. So a linked worktree of a bare repository opens, except when extensions.worktreeConfig makes the common core.bare apply to it. The reader makes these checks each time it opens a worktree. The lint just lint bans the write paths of the gix crates (GIT-03). tests/git_reader.rs checks that a run of every call leaves the Git directories unchanged. tests/git_write_lint.rs checks that no other source file names a gix path.

Git’s SYMREF_MAXDEPTH is five. commit_bytes u64 Maximum bytes of one commit object, after decompression. parents usize Maximum number of parents of one commit. alternates_bytes u64 Maximum bytes of each objects/info/alternates file. alternates usize Maximum number of alternate object directories, over all nested alternates files. text: source pub enum GitReadError GitReadError names each reason why the reader refuses or fails, with what the user must know. Variant Description Io { path: PathBuf, cause: Cause } A file system call failed. NotAWorktree { path: PathBuf } The folder has no .git entry and is not a Git directory. NotARepository { path: PathBuf, cause: Cause } The .git entry does not lead to a valid Git directory. Bare { path: PathBuf } The folder is a bare repository, which is not a location (SRC-09). Shallow { common_dir: PathBuf } The repository is a shallow clone, which the first release refuses (P10). Reftable { common_dir: PathBuf } The repository uses the reftable ref backend, which the first release refuses. UnsupportedObjectFormat { value: Vec  } extensions.objectFormat names a format other than sha1 or sha256. UnsupportedRefStorage { value: Vec  } extensions.refStorage names a backend other than files or reftable. UnsupportedRepositoryVersion { version: i64 } core.repositoryformatversion is not 0 or 1, or is 0 with a version-1 extension. ForeignWorktree { worktree: PathBuf, configured: PathBuf } core.worktree names a folder other than the opened one, so Git’s worktree is elsewhere. UnsupportedExtension { name: String } Version 1 names an extension that the reader does not understand, which Git also refuses. Config { path: PathBuf, cause: Cause } A configuration file or value could not be parsed. TooLarge { what: String, size: u64, limit: u64 } A file or object is larger than its limit. NotAFile { path: PathBuf, kind: &'static str } An entry that must be a regular file is a FIFO, a device, a socket, a folder, or a symbolic link that the reader does not follow. Alternate { path: PathBuf, cause: Cause } An objects/info/alternates file names an alternate that the reader does not use, or the alternates changed after the open. InvalidObjectId { text: String, format: ObjectFormat } A text is not a full object ID of the format. FormatMismatch { id: GitObjectId, repository: ObjectFormat } An object ID has a format other than the format of the repository. InvalidBranchName { name: String } A branch name does not make a valid full ref name. Ref { name: Vec , cause: Cause } A ref could not be read or parsed. SymbolicDepth { name: Vec , limit: usize } A chain of symbolic refs is deeper than the limit. ObjectRead { id: GitObjectId, cause: Cause } The object store failed to read an object. ObjectMissing { id: GitObjectId } No object with the ID is present, not even in an alternate (COMP-T06). NotACommit { id: GitObjectId, kind: ObjectKind } The object exists, but it is not a commit. HashMismatch { id: GitObjectId, computed: GitObjectId } The recomputed hash of the object differs from its ID. MalformedCommit { id: GitObjectId, cause: Cause } The commit body could not be parsed up to its parents. TooManyParents { id: GitObjectId, limit: usize } The commit has more parents than the limit. Implements Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Display, Error.

text: source pub fn open(worktree: &Path, limits: Limits) -> Result  Open the Git worktree whose top folder is worktree, and check that the first release supports it. The folder must hold the .git entry itself. The reader searches no parent folder and reads no Git environment variable.

title: git_reader
text: Returns one of these errors: GitReadError::NotAWorktree for a folder without a .git entry. GitReadError::NotARepository for a .git entry that leads to no valid Git directory, a .git file whose path ends in whitespace, or a .git file that names no folder. GitReadError::Shallow, GitReadError::Reftable, GitReadError::Bare, GitReadError::ForeignWorktree or GitReadError::UnsupportedExtension. GitReadError::TooLarge for a HEAD, a .git file or commondir over small_file_bytes, for a configuration file over config_bytes, or for an alternates file over alternates_bytes. GitReadError::NotAFile for one of those entries that is a FIFO, a device, a socket, a dangling or refused symbolic link, or a folder other than .git. GitReadError::Ref for a HEAD that cannot be parsed. GitReadError::NotARepository also for a HEAD that names a ref outside refs/, or a commondir that is empty after its line ends. GitReadError::Alternate for alternates over the count or the depth, an alternate that is not a folder, a quoted path, a relative path in a nested alternates file, or a folder that appears twice. GitReadError::Config for a configuration that cannot be parsed. An error for an unsupported format or version, or for a read error.

title: git_reader
text: use gossil::git_reader::{GitReadError, GitRepository, Head, Limits}; use std::path::Path; /// Return the parents of the commit at `HEAD`, or `None` for an unborn branch. fn head_parents(worktree: &Path) -> Result >, GitReadError> { let repo = GitRepository::open(worktree, Limits::STANDARD)?; let tip = match repo.head()? { Head::Branch { tip, .. } => tip, Head::Detached(id) => Some(id), }; let Some(tip) = tip else { return Ok(None) }; let commit = repo.read_commit(&tip)?; Ok(Some(commit.parents().iter().map(|id| id.to_hex()).collect())) } // A folder without a `.git` entry is not a worktree. The open searches no parent folder. let folder = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap(); let error = head_parents(folder.path()).unwrap_err(); assert!(matches!(error, GitReadError::NotAWorktree { .. })); Parameter Type Description worktree &Path Top folder of a main or linked worktree. limits Limits Bounds of this call and of every later call. returns Result  The opened repository.

title: glob
text: Lists use comma and ASCII-whitespace delimiters. A leading single or double quote retains delimiters until the same closing quote; an unmatched quote consumes the remaining prefix. There is no quote escape syntax. Every input ends at its first NUL. Matching returns the first one-based index, or zero. glob_expr retains a distinct extra byte advance after a closing quote. Its value argument is trusted SQL. Bind untrusted candidate values separately. These functions perform no traversal, settings lookup or tracking mutation.

title: glob
text: Use glob_create for repeated matching and glob_multi_match for one scan. Next, set explicit byte/count budgets and bind candidate values separately when executing SQL from glob_expr.

title: glob
text: source pub struct Limits Supply finite byte/count budgets; input byte lengths stop before the first NUL. Prefix detection itself scans the original slice until NUL or its end. These budgets do not impose a separate CPU-time or stack limit. Field Type Description list_bytes usize Maximum pattern-list bytes. candidate_bytes usize Maximum candidate bytes. patterns usize Maximum number of parsed patterns. expression_bytes usize Maximum SQL expression bytes, including the caller’s value expression. Implements Clone, Copy, Debug.

Overflow Capacity arithmetic overflowed. Allocation(TryReserveError) Fallible reservation failed. Implements Debug, Display, Error.

title: glob
text: source pub fn glob_create(list: Option , limits: Limits) -> Result  Parse a reusable Fossil pattern list; absent or delimiter-only lists match nothing. Only an initial quote opens a quoted term. Commas and ASCII whitespace delimit unquoted terms, unmatched quotes consume the remainder, and empty quoted terms remain patterns. The list ends at its first NUL; no escape syntax is applied.

title: glob
text: Returns GlobError::Limit when list bytes or pattern count exceed their budgets, GlobError::Overflow for capacity arithmetic, or GlobError::Allocation when reservation fails. Parameter Type Description list Option  Optional pattern list; None has the same meaning as an empty list. limits Limits Finite input, pattern and output budgets. returns Result  Owned parsed patterns and the retained candidate budget.

title: glob
text: source pub fn glob_multi_match( list: Option , candidate: &[u8], limits: Limits, ) -> Result  Match a Fossil list once and return the first one-based match index, or zero. A matching term returns immediately, without checking later terms against the pattern-count limit. Terms below 100 bytes use a temporary stack buffer; longer terms use a fallible allocation. Neither choice bounds engine recursion.

title: glob
text: Returns GlobError::Limit when list bytes, candidate bytes or an inspected pattern count exceed their budgets, GlobError::Overflow for terminator capacity arithmetic, or GlobError::Allocation when reservation fails.

title: glob
text: use gossil::glob::{glob_multi_match, Limits}; let limits = Limits { list_bytes: 64, candidate_bytes: 64, patterns: 1, expression_bytes: 256 }; // Early success does not inspect the second term against the count budget. assert_eq!(glob_multi_match(Some(b"a*,b*"), b"abc", limits)?, 1); assert!(glob_multi_match(Some(b"a*,b*"), b"zzz", limits).is_err()); Parameter Type Description list Option  Optional pattern list, ending at the first NUL. candidate &[u8] Candidate bytes, ending at the first NUL. limits Limits Finite input, pattern and output budgets. returns Result  The first matching one-based pattern index, or zero when no pattern matches.

title: glob
text: source pub fn glob_expr(value: &[u8], list: Option , limits: Limits) -> Result , GlobError> Build a SQL expression from trusted SQL and Fossil patterns, with native quote advancement. The caller MUST supply a trusted SQL value expression. Only pattern apostrophes are escaped; value is neither quoted nor sanitized. Never pass untrusted SQL. Use a trusted column or parameter expression such as b"?1" and bind candidate bytes separately when executing the result through a caller-owned SQL interface. This function executes no SQL. All input slices end at their first NUL. Empty, absent and delimiter-only lists return b"0"; a quoted empty pattern produces a real GLOB term. Adjacent text after a closing quote can therefore differ from glob_create and glob_multi_match parsing.

title: glob
text: Returns GlobError::Limit when list bytes, pattern count or expression bytes exceed their budgets, GlobError::Overflow for output capacity arithmetic, or GlobError::Allocation when reservation fails.

title: glob
text: use gossil::glob::{glob_expr, Limits}; let limits = Limits { list_bytes: 64, candidate_bytes: 64, patterns: 8, expression_bytes: 256 }; // Bind the candidate separately when executing this trusted parameter expression. assert_eq!(glob_expr(b"?1", Some(b"*.rs"), limits)?, b"(?1 GLOB '*.rs')"); assert_eq!(glob_expr(b"?1", None, limits)?, b"0"); Parameter Type Description value &[u8] Trusted SQL expression, neither quoted nor sanitized. list Option  Optional pattern list, ending at the first NUL. limits Limits Finite input, pattern and expression budgets. returns Result , GlobError> SQL expression bytes, or b"0" when the list has no patterns.

title: history
text: The original code is copyright 2011 D. Richard Hipp, under the 2-Clause BSD license. The license text is in tests/fixtures/history/fossil-license.txt. The module ports path_shortest, path_common_ancestor and the queue order of pqueue.c from Fossil check-in 7e8ecf0ce4, over rows that the caller supplies. It neither reads a repository nor grants authority to derived indexes. Callers supply the query order of the plink and cherrypick rows, and the resolved metadata of branch and time. The algorithms keep the tie order of pqueue.c, and the native ban on a backwards step after a forward edge. The bounds and the errors for malformed input are new controls.

Returns the failure exit code after printing an adapter error to standard error. A repository at an older Gossil catalog returns 78. The first argument v is accepted as an alias for vcs. text: source pub async fn verify_issue( &mut self, id: &str, limits: AdmissionLimits, ) -> Result  Prove one task or project from its own rows. The ticket whose gest_id names the ID must be the only one. The proof then replays its one artifact and compares its event, tagxref, ticket, ticketchng and combined typed rows with that replay. It refuses a row of the unsent, unclustered, leaf, phantom, orphan, backlink, attachment, mlink or plink table that names the artifact or the ticket. It replays no other artifact. For a task it checks only that a combined project row with its project ID exists. When none does, it refuses with a stored task names a project that the repository does not hold, although the full proof admits such a task. It changes nothing. The one lookup of the ticket by its Gest ID scans the ticket table. The other reads use an index or a primary key. The proof checks that each table that the full proof keeps empty in every repository has no row, with one fixed query per table. The proof does not see a row that no index of the issue reaches, or a typed row in another scope.

title: task_ticket
text: See the task ticket guide for the format, caller responsibilities and a library example. The shared emitter of crate::gest_ticket writes the bytes. This module gives it the task’s eleven model fields and the kind task, and re-exports its TicketError. Card order and token/checksum construction follow Fossil tkt.c:1837-1874 (b3a1c8efb2731dffbd5cc38c58ac349746de6da6). Fossil is Copyright D. Richard Hipp and contributors; its BSD two-clause license is preserved in the frozen source evidence. This module performs no storage, identity generation or admission. Re-exports TicketError.

title: task_ticket
text: source pub fn task_creation_bytes( task: &TaskValues, ticket_id: &[u8], actor: &[u8], date: NativeDate, max_output: usize, ) -> Result , TicketError> Emit complete uncompressed Fossil ticket artifact bytes for a validated task creation. The caller supplies the K card’s ticket identity, actor bytes and a validated creation date. K is forty lowercase ASCII hexadecimal bytes, independent of the 32-character Gest ID in the task. Actor bytes need not be UTF-8 or a Gest author ID. crate::gest_task_values supplies the normalized status spelling and UTC timestamp strings. All eleven model fields use JSON followed by native token escaping. The three additional J fields are gossil_deleted=false, raw gossil_kind=task and raw gossil_schema=1. The fourteen J fields are sorted by name. No append or parent card is emitted. The caller manages history and enforces any requirement that artifact creation dates increase. max_output bounds complete encoded bytes, including the final checksum and newline, with an effective ceiling of isize::MAX. It is not a heap budget. The emitter counts token-escaped JSON bytes before retaining serialized JSON or reserving output bytes.

title: gest_model
text: This module ports src/store/model of Gest at commit eaf821b19c3cf75b99d22e1cc70e0eff4a3562a8, under the MIT licence in src/gest_model/gest-LICENSE.txt. Each submodule keeps the upstream name of its Model struct and of its New, Patch and Filter inputs. The port differs from upstream in these ways: There is no TryFrom . Gossil does not store Gest SQL rows. A model comes from a record that a converter in crate::gest_*_values has validated, through From, so the converters stay the one place that checks a decoded field. The models also derive Deserialize, as upstream does. The project_workspace and transaction models are not here. They are local bookkeeping, and the storage tasks own them. Getters are written by hand, with the names and return types that the getset derives give upstream. The clock comes from std::time::SystemTime, as chrono::Utc::now does, so chrono needs no clock feature. Name Summary artifact Represent a project document, such as a spec or an ADR. The artifacts table: a project’s documents, such as specs and ADRs. author Represent the humans and agents who write notes and other records. The authors table: the humans and agents who create notes, events and other records. entity_tag Represent the attachment of a tag to a task, an artifact or an iteration. The entity_tags join table, which attaches a tag to a task, an artifact or an iteration. iteration Represent a time-boxed group of tasks. The iterations table: time-boxed groups of tasks within a project. note Represent a note attached to an entity. The notes table: notes attached to an entity, each with an optional author. primitives Hold the primitive values that the Gest records use. project Represent a tracked project. The projects table: each repository or directory root that Gest tracks. relationship Represent a directed link between two entities. The relationships table: directed links, such as blocks or child-of, between two entities. tag Represent a label that is stored once and attached to entities. The tags table: labels, stored once each, that the entity_tags table attaches to entities. task Represent a unit of work within a project. The tasks table: units of work within a project. Re-exports Author, Project, Tag.

title: primitives
text: source pub struct Id(/* private field */); A 128-bit identifier encoded as a 32-character string using the k-z alphabet. Each byte is split into two nibbles and mapped through a reverse-hex alphabet, producing a lowercase, URL-safe string that sorts in reverse byte order. The encoding is bijective. Every valid 32-character [k-z] string decodes to exactly one [u8; 16], and each [u8; 16] encodes to exactly one such string.
